label: S0377
statement:
statement: One-hot prefix transducer upper bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For each t, let P_t be the live prefixes of length t and L_t=|P_t|. There is an exact full-search streaming transducer with S=max_t L_t state bits, one-hot states for live prefixes and the all-zero state for dead prefixes, and at most G_max=max_t min(L_t,L_{t+1}) + 1 gates per update in the basis {AND, XOR, NOT, constants}; its final decoder maps the one-hot state of a full-length prefix f to f (or its witness circuit, if each f is supplied with a fixed witness), and maps zero to rejection. Proof: assign each live prefix p at time t a distinct unit vector e_p in {0,1}^S, and assign every dead prefix the zero vector. Given a live prefix p and next bit b, its child pb is either live or dead. For every live child q of length t+1, there is exactly one possible predecessor p=q without its last bit and one bit b equal to q's last bit. Set output coordinate q to (input coordinate p) AND b when that bit is 1, and to (input coordinate p) AND NOT b when it is 0. The shared NOT b costs at most one gate; each live child output costs one AND gate. On a live input state these equations produce its live child’s unit vector, or zero if the child is dead; on zero they produce zero. Thus every transition is correct on all reachable states and all dead prefixes remain at zero. The final decoder is exact by construction. The maximum number of AND gates at step t is L_{t+1}, so the stated bound holds. This bound is only an upper bound and does not establish a fixed S<N point for SC_{3,1}; for the listed SC_{3,1} profile it uses S=max_t L_t=38, so it does not close the assigned fixed-frame gap.

label: S0400
statement: statement: Singleton streaming upper bound. For every N>=1 and fixed w in {0,1}^N, F={w} has a deterministic time-varying full-search transducer with one state bit, q_0=1, at most two {AND,NOT} gates per update, and a one-bit final decoder, correct on every input. At time t set q_t=q_{t-1} AND x_t when w_t=1, and q_t=q_{t-1} AND (NOT x_t) when w_t=0. Induction gives q_t=1 exactly when the input prefix equals w[1..t]. Thus each live prefix has state 1, all dead prefixes state 0, and q_N decides membership in F. Each update uses at most one AND and one NOT. This is only a constructive upper bound for singleton target families; it says nothing about SC_{n,s} or optimality.

label: S0482
statement:
statement: Repetition-code streaming membership upper bound. For every N>=2, let F={0^N,1^N} subset {0,1}^N. There is an exact deterministic one-pass membership transducer with S=2 state bits, a fixed final decoder, and at most two non-constant fan-in-two AND/XOR gates per update (NOT and constants free; shared fan-out free).
proof: Use state (a,l), where a stores the first input bit and l is the live flag. Initially use (0,0). On the first bit b, set the next state to (b,1) by wiring, so this update uses no gates. On every later bit b, preserve a and set l' = l AND NOT(a XOR b); this uses one XOR gate to compute a XOR b and one AND gate. By induction after t>=1 bits, l=1 exactly when all t bits equal a, and a equals the first bit. The decoder accepts iff l=1 after N bits. Therefore it accepts exactly 0^N and 1^N. The state has two bits, every update has at most two counted gates, and the construction is valid for every N>=2.
scope: An explicit upper bound in the fan-in-two AND/XOR/NOT-free basis for the two-word repetition language. It does not bound SC_{n,s}, arbitrary encodings, or a general lower bound on update cost.

structure.evidence: A direct invariant proof supplies a correct transducer and its per-step gate count; no finite synthesis result or asymptotic lower-bound inference is used.

label: S0517
statement:
statement: Singleton-language streaming upper bound. For every N>=1 and w in {0,1}^N, the language F={w} has a deterministic one-pass membership machine with one state bit, free NOT and constants, fan-in-two AND gates, and at most one AND gate per update.
proof: Initialize q=1. At position i, set q'=q when w_i=1 and q'=q AND NOT(b) when w_i=0. Inductively q=1 after t bits exactly when the input prefix equals w_1...w_t. Accept iff q=1 after N bits. Hence exactly w is accepted; each update uses at most one AND gate.
scope: Singleton finite binary languages; one state bit; fixed length and position-dependent transitions; membership only.

label: S0518
statement: statement: Two-candidate streaming upper bound. For every N>=1 and every two-element set F={u,v} subset {0,1}^N, there is a deterministic one-pass exact membership transducer with two state bits and at most two fan-in-two AND gates per update (NOT and constants free; fixed layer-dependent transitions; unrestricted final decoder). Initialize the state (a,b)=(1,1). At position i on input bit z, update (a,b) to (a AND [z=u_i], b AND [z=v_i]); each bracket is a literal of z, implemented by z or NOT z, so each output uses at most one AND gate. After t positions, a=1 iff the read prefix equals u_1...u_t, and b=1 iff it equals v_1...v_t, by induction. At t=N, the input belongs to F iff a OR b=1, so the decoder accepts exactly F. Thus the update gate bound is two at every position. This proves an upper bound for two-word languages only and gives no lower bound for SC_{n,s}.

statement: statement: For every binary matrix A of rank r with r rows and every b in F_2^r, the affine language F={x in {0,1}^N: Ax=b} has a one-pass streaming membership machine with r state bits, initial state 0, at most r XOR gates per update, and final equality decoder. label: S0638
statement:
statement: For every binary stream x of length N, there is a layered one-pass transducer with S=N state bits, zero nonconstant update gates in the AND/XOR/NOT basis with free wires and time-dependent updates, and a terminal decoder that outputs x exactly. At layer t, the state is (x_1,...,x_t,0,...,0).
proof: Initialize all N state bits to zero. At step t, wire the current input bit into state coordinate t and wire every other coordinate unchanged. The update schedule knows t, so this uses no nonconstant Boolean gates. By induction, after t steps the first t coordinates equal the consumed prefix and the remaining coordinates are zero. At t=N the state equals x, so the decoder outputs x exactly.
scope: All fixed-length binary streams; arbitrary time-dependent layered updates and free wires. This proves only the S=N endpoint; it gives no result for S<N or minimal decoder cost.

label: S0840
statement:
statement: For every finite witness relation R ⊆ {0,1}^N × W, there is a deterministic layered transducer that reads the input in order, uses S=N state bits, has zero non-constant update gates at every step, and whose final decoder accepts exactly inputs x for which some w satisfies (x,w) ∈ R, outputting one such witness. At layer t, store the t-bit prefix in the first t state bits and set the remaining N−t bits to zero. On input b, the next state copies the current prefix bits, appends b, and leaves the rest zero. These updates use only wires and constants. At layer N the state equals x, so the decoder can apply any fixed choice function selecting a witness for each accepted x, and reject otherwise. This is an exact construction for arbitrary finite R; it gives no bound when the state budget is smaller than N or when decoder complexity is charged.
scope: Finite input length N, arbitrary finite witness set W and relation R, unrestricted final decoder, state budget S=N, AND/XOR/NOT updates with wires and constants free.

structure.evidence: Direct construction and verification: after t transitions the state contains exactly the consumed prefix followed by zeros; hence the final decoder receives the original input unchanged. This does not address the binding Lemma M state budget or its exact G_max synthesis.

label: S0022
statement: LEMMA (subclass, bounded top fan-in, O2 of PNP-001-THR-SAT-2026-11-21). Let f(x) = [sum_{j in S} v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T] with |S| = k, integer weights |W_{j,i}| <= B, integer thresholds t_j and integer v_j. Then #f = |{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1}| is computed exactly by the DP that keeps, after each variable i, a multiplicity table over the vectors (W_j . x_{<=i})_{j in S}. PROOF: at step i the table maps each vector y in Z^k to #{x_{<=i} : partial sums = y}; the step x_i in {0,1} adds 0 or the column (W_{j,i})_{j in S}, so the recurrence is exact by induction on i. At the end f depends on x only through the final vector, so summing the multiplicities of vectors that satisfy the top threshold gives #f. Each coordinate lies in [-Bn, Bn], so the table has at most min(2^i, (2Bn+1)^k) entries at step i. Total time O(k n min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^k)) arithmetic operations. CONSEQUENCES: (a) k = O(1): time n^{O(k)} (polynomial). (b) If k log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta) n, time 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n). SCOPE: exact count for bounded top fan-in only. It does not bound approximate rank for the full class and does not close G0002.

structure.evidence: Exactness: physalis_code_run cm-aacbae4be3e64bd3 (200 random instances, n in 3..10, k in 1..3, weights in [-3,3]; DP vs brute force, 0 failures). Running time: exploratory only until thr2_evaluate (sharp_sat) reports it, which I am submitting now.

It is not a balanced-split or variable-tree rank bound for unbounded top fan-in, and it is not a CAPP algorithm for XOR_2 o THR o THR of size n^alpha with unbounded top fan-in. Open: whether a sub-exponential or 2^{n}/n^{omega(1)} saving holds with unbounded k under a constructible order.

label: S0027
statement: SUBCLASS LEMMA (exact counting, #SAT of THR o THR with few distinct bottom forms). Setting: f(z) = [sum_{j<=m} v_j [w_j.z >= t_j] >= T], integer weights w_j in {-W..W}^n, t_j, v_j, T integers. Let f_1..f_r be the DISTINCT weight vectors among the w_j, and sigma(j) the index with w_j = f_{sigma(j)}. Let h = floor(n/2), X = first h variables, Y = the remaining n-h. Then #f = sum over a in Z^r of N_X(a) * G(a), where N_X(a) = #{x in {0,1}^h : (f_i.x)_i = a} and G(a) = #{y in {0,1}^(n-h) : sum_j v_j [B_{sigma(j)}(y) + a_{sigma(j)} >= t_j] >= T}, B_i(y) = f_i restricted to Y . y. PROOF: w_j.(x,y) = f_{sigma(j)}.x + f_{sigma(j)}.y = a_{sigma(j)}(x) + B_{sigma(j)}(y), so the gate test depends on x only through a(x) in Z^r, and the summand depends on x only through a(x). Summing over x grouped by a(x) gives the formula. The number of a with N_X(a) > 0 is at most min(2^h, (2Wh+1)^r), since each coordinate a_i(x) lies in [-Wh, Wh]. RUNNING TIME: computing N_X takes 2^h * poly(n,r) time; each class a costs (n-h)-enumeration 2^(n-h) * m * poly. Total time = poly(n,m) * (2^(n/2) + min(2^(n/2), (2Wh+1)^r) * 2^(n/2)) <= poly(m,n) * 2^(n/2) * min(2^(n/2), (2Wn+1)^r). For FIXED r and W (or W = poly(n) with fixed r) this is 2^(n/2) * poly(n), i.e. a saving of 2^(n/2)/poly(n) = 2^n / n^{omega(1)} over brute force, for exact #f. EXTENSION: for XOR of two such circuits (the CAPP class of Chen-Tal-Wang Lemma 3.8) the same argument with r1 + r2 forms gives an exact deterministic count of Pr[C1 XOR C2 = 1] in 2^(n/2) * (2Wn+1)^(r1+r2) * poly time, i.e. error 0 with no approximation. SCOPE / LIMITS: holds only for circuits with r = O(1) distinct bottom weight vectors (or poly-size weight range with r fixed); it does NOT address G0002 (O-R), G0003-G0010 (full-rank / random instances with r = m), and it does not show that the subclass contains the hard functions of Lemma 3.8 (open). The saving is only for this subclass; no statement about the class with r = n^1.5 distinct forms. Correctness and sample running time to be checked by thr2_evaluate/physalis_code_run cm-576409d3a2664050 (60 rows, n<=14, all correct, D within bound).

label: S0052
statement: statement: CONDITIONAL BALANCED-SPLIT CONSEQUENCE. Fix a family of THR∘THR instances with n input bits, total encoding length L=poly(n), integer bottom weights bounded by W≤n^c for a fixed c, and a balanced split X|Y with h=|X|=⌊n/2⌋. If the rational rank q of the distinct restricted bottom weight vectors on X satisfies q=o(n/log n), then exact #SAT is computable in 2^{n/2+o(n)} time. Proof: enumerate all 2^h assignments x and tabulate multiplicities by their restricted-form signatures. The signature bound gives at most K=min(2^h,(2Wh+1)^q) signatures. For each signature enumerate all 2^{n-h} assignments y, evaluate the m bottom gates and top threshold in poly(L,n,m) time per pair, and add the signature multiplicity for each accepting y. This is exact because each x in a bucket has identical restricted bottom-form values, so for every y each bottom gate and the output agree. Since W≤n^c, log2 K≤q log2(2Wh+1)=o(n); hence the work is poly(n)(2^{n/2}+2^{n/2+o(n)})=2^{n/2+o(n)}. This is a conditional subclass algorithm and makes no claim for unrestricted q.

Proof: enumerate all 2^h assignments x and tabulate multiplicities by their restricted-form signatures. The signature bound gives at most K=min(2^h,(2Wh+1)^q) signatures. For each signature enumerate all 2^{n-h} assignments y, evaluate the m bottom gates and top threshold in poly(L,n,m) time per pair, and add the signature multiplicity for each accepting y. This is exact because each x in a bucket has identical restricted bottom-form values, so for every y each bottom gate and the output agree. statement:
statement: Rank-one split lemma: Given a THR∘THR circuit with split X|Y, |X|=h, integer X-weights |a_ji|≤W and rational rank({a_j})≤1, exact #SAT takes poly(L,n,m)(2^h+(2Wh+1)2^(n−h)) time. Proof: If all a_j=0, use one bucket. Otherwise choose nonzero b among a_j. Rank one gives a_j=λ_jb over Q, so each a_j·x is determined by b·x. Thus for fixed y, all bottom gate values and the top output are constant on each bucket of equal b·x. Since b is integer with |b_i|≤W, b·x has at most 2Wh+1 values. Enumerate x into buckets, enumerate y once per bucket and weight accepted y by the bucket size; this counts each satisfying pair exactly once. The work is the stated enumeration count times polynomial circuit-evaluation cost. For h=floor(n/2) and W≤n^c, the time is 2^(n/2)poly(L,n,m).

label: S0060
statement: GCD-SPACED SIGNATURE ALGORITHM. Let A be the distinct integer X-weight rows of a THR∘THR circuit on split X|Y, |X|=h, with rational rank q. Select q independent rows b_i and let g_i=gcd(|(b_i)_1|,...,|(b_i)_h|)>0. Put K=min(2^h, product_i(floor(||b_i||_1/g_i)+1)); for q=0 set K=1. The number of full restricted signatures (a·x)_{a∈A} is at most K. Consequently exact #SAT is computable in O(poly(L,n,m)(2^h+K2^{n-h})) time by bucketing X assignments by full signature and enumerating Y once per bucket. Proof: each b_i·x is a multiple of g_i in an interval of length ||b_i||_1, hence it has at most floor(||b_i||_1/g_i)+1 values. The q basis values determine every a·x because each a is a rational linear combination of the b_i; therefore the joint signature count is at most their product and at most 2^h. For each bucket, all restricted linear forms have fixed values; fixing y then fixes every bottom threshold and the top threshold, so enumeration of y and weighting accepted y by the bucket size counts satisfying pairs exactly. Constructing buckets costs O(poly(L,n,m)2^h), and the enumerations cost O(poly(L,n,m)K2^{n-h}). In particular, if the displayed product is 2^{o(n)} on a balanced split and h=floor(n/2), runtime is 2^{n/2+o(n)}. This is a conditional subclass algorithm; it gives no bound when the product is large.

label: S0546
statement:
statement: IMAGE-SIZE RECODING LEMMA. Let Q be an m-element set, S=ceil(log2 m), and delta:Q->Q have image size k>=1. There is an injective stationary encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that exactly ceil(log2 k) output coordinates of psi(delta(q)) are nonconstant as q ranges over Q. Consequently the partial transition psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) has a total extension computable by O(2^S ceil(log2 k)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (and zero gates when k=1).
proof: Choose k distinct codes for the elements of im(delta) to be 0,1,...,k-1, and let r=ceil(log2 k). Every such code has zero bits in positions r,...,S-1, so those S-r output coordinates are constant on the image. To obtain an injection on all of Q, assign the m-k remaining elements distinct unused S-bit codes; there are 2^S-k such codes and 2^S>=m. For each of the r possibly varying output coordinates, prescribe its values on the encoded states psi(Q), and extend it arbitrarily to all 2^S input strings. Shannon expansion on S input bits realizes each total Boolean coordinate function with at most 2^S-1 two-input muxes, each mux using a constant number of AND/NOT gates. Extend the other coordinates by their constant image value, requiring no gates. Thus the total is O(r 2^S); when k=1, r=0 and every transition output coordinate is constant on encoded states, so constant extensions compute the partial transition at zero gate cost. Since 2^S<2m for m>=2, this is O(m ceil(log2 k)).

label: S0647
statement:
statement_start: LEMMA: Cyclic successor on the standard S-bit encoding, S=ceil(log2 m), has a fan-in-2 circuit of size O(S).
evidence: For valid x in [0,m), compute y=x+1 mod 2^S and e=[x=m-1]. Output z_i=y_i AND NOT e for each bit. A fan-in-2 incrementer, equality test against a constant, and output masking each use O(S) gates. For x<m-1 this gives x+1; for x=m-1 it gives 0. Thus the circuit implements cyclic successor on valid encodings in O(S)=O(log m) gates. This proves only an upper bound for the standard encoding.

label: S0363
statement: LEMMA S (exact residual streaming for EXT). Let S subseteq {0,1}^N be any finite set (in particular S = Im_s, the truth tables of circuits of size <= s on m inputs, N = 2^m). For a prefix p of length t define the residual R_t(p) = {q in {0,1}^{N-t} : p q in S}. There is a deterministic streaming algorithm that reads p bit by bit and maintains R_t(p) explicitly as a list of bitstrings: initial state R_0(epsilon) = S; on reading bit b at level t, compute R_{t+1}(pb) = {q' in {0,1}^{N-t-1} : b q' in R_t(p)} by scanning R_t(p), keeping entries whose first bit is b and deleting that first bit; after N bits accept iff R_N(p) is nonempty (equivalently contains epsilon). PROOF OF CORRECTNESS by induction on t. Base t=0: R_0(epsilon) = S = {q : epsilon q in S}. Inductive step: assume R_t(p) = {q : p q in S}. Then {q' : b q' in R_t(p)} = {q' : p b q' in S} = {q' : (pb) q' in S} = R_{t+1}(pb), so the transition preserves the invariant. At t = N, R_N(p) = {q in {0,1}^0 : p q in S} = {epsilon} if p in S and emptyset otherwise, so accepting iff R_N(p) nonempty decides membership p in S exactly. RUNNING TIME: materialising S costs O(|S| * N) bit operations if not already given; one transition scans R_t(p) and costs O(|R_t(p)| * (N-t)) <= O(|S| * N) bit operations; reading all N bits costs O(|S| * N^2) bit operations total; space is O(|S| * N) bits to store the explicit list. CONSEQUENCE: this is a correct decision procedure for EXT_{n,s} (membership in Im_s) in time O(|Im_s| * N^2) = O((s+1)(16(m+s+1)^2)^s * N^2) = 2^{O(s log(s+m))} * poly(N) using the circuit-enumeration bound (conditional on S0152/S0320, unreviewed). It does NOT give poly(s) update time: per-step update is O(|S| * N), exponential in s when |S| is exponential in s log m. Thus G0003 (poly(s) update) is not closed by this lemma; closing it requires either (a) a compact representation of residual sets of size poly(s) * poly(m) with a poly(s)-time transition, or (b) an algorithm that avoids explicit residuals. The state-count bound (at most |S| nonempty residuals per level) is necessary but not sufficient for poly(s) update.

structure.evidence: Mathematical proof by induction on prefix length; the per-step transition and cost follow directly from the residual definition. Shrinks gap G0004 from 'is the transition computable' to 'can residuals be represented compactly enough'; explicitly does not close G0003.

label: S0582
statement:
statement: SIMULTANEOUS BLOCK-COFACTOR CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} have a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, with constants and input wiring free. For integers 0<=t<=N and 0<=b<=N-t, set k=N-t-b. There is a fan-in-two circuit with t input bits p and 2^b outputs indexed by u in {0,1}^b, whose u-output is 1 iff some v in {0,1}^k satisfies H(puv)=1. Its gate count is at most 2^{N-t}h+2^{N-t}-2^b. Proof: for every pair (u,v), make a disjoint copy of H with first t inputs wired to p and remaining inputs fixed to uv, giving 2^{b+k}h=2^{N-t}h gates. For each u, OR its 2^k outputs using a fan-in-two tree of 2^k-1 gates (zero gates if k=0), giving 2^b(2^k-1)=2^{N-t}-2^b further gates. The output for u computes the required existential cofactor; summing gives the bound. Direct enumeration makes the construction uniform. This is a per-cut construction only, not a polynomial early-cut bound or an MCSP lower bound.
scope: All N-bit Boolean circuits H and cuts/blocks 0<=t, 0<=b<=N-t; fan-in-two gate size, constants and wiring free.
evidence: Complete copy-and-OR derivation; no finite computation is used.

label: S0592
statement: statement: Explicit circuit construction for prefix extension. Let N>=0, F subseteq {0,1}^N, and let H be a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size h and depth d deciding membership in F. For a prefix p of length t and k=N-t remaining bits, an exact circuit deciding whether p has an accepted completion is obtained by instantiating H on each of the 2^k strings pu and ORing the outputs in a binary tree. Its size is at most 2^k h+(2^k-1) and its depth is at most d+k. Proof: for each u in {0,1}^k, the corresponding copy outputs 1 exactly when pu is in F. Their disjunction is 1 exactly when some completion belongs to F. There are 2^k copies, costing 2^k h gates, and a binary OR tree on 2^k outputs uses 2^k-1 gates and depth k (with the k=0 case using one copy and no OR gates). This supplies a real-gate upper-bound baseline from an arbitrary complete-input decider; it gives no matching lower bound for structured EXT_{n,s}.

label: S0599
statement:
statement: Explicit witness-mask update bound for EXT. Fix n,s and a finite enumerated circuit family C_{n,s} of size M, with each circuit’s truth-table bits in a fixed order. Encode the current prefix residual by an M-bit vector z, where z_j=1 exactly when circuit j agrees with the prefix read so far. For each position i and input bit b, the next-state vector is z'_j=z_j AND [bit_i(C_j)=b]. This is an exact deterministic update using at most M binary AND gates (the bracketed values are constants), and the state uses M bits. Initially z is all ones; after the full truth table, z is nonzero exactly when the input belongs to EXT_{n,s}. Proof: Inductively, after t bits z_j=1 iff circuit j agrees with the first t bits. The displayed update preserves that invariant for t+1 by testing precisely the next bit. At t=N, nonemptiness is equivalent to existence of a size-at-most-s circuit generating the input truth table. This gives an explicit O(M)-gate per-bit upper bound for the witness-set representation; it does not give a bound polynomial in s, nor a construction from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
scope: Finite explicitly enumerated circuit families with fixed truth-table ordering; deterministic exact streaming; gate count is for the update with circuit truth-table bits available as constants, and M=|C_{n,s}|.

label: S0842
statement: FINITE-FAMILY PREFIX UPDATE BOUND. Fix N,s and a finite indexed family F=(f_1,...,f_M) of Boolean functions on {0,1}^N, each given by a fan-in-two circuit of at most s gates; fix an ordering a_0,...,a_{2^N-1} of {0,1}^N. At time t (0<=t<=2^N), let I_p={i: (f_i(a_0),...,f_i(a_{t-1}))=p} for p in {0,1}^t. The exact transition on next input bit b is I_{pb}={i in I_p:f_i(a_t)=b}. If every value f_i(a_t) is computed from its circuit, a Boolean circuit for the transition from the M membership bits of I_p to the M membership bits of I_{pb} has at most Ms+M gates for b=1 and at most Ms+2M gates for b=0, using AND, NOT, and the indicated circuit copies; it has at most Ms+2M gates uniformly. Proof: Compute each selector v_i=f_i(a_t) with a copy of the at-most-s-gate circuit f_i after substituting constants a_t, costing at most Ms gates total. For each i output q_i AND v_i when b=1, or q_i AND NOT(v_i) when b=0, where q_i is the old membership bit; this costs at most M gates for b=1 and 2M for b=0. By the definition of I_p, i belongs to I_{pb} exactly when it belongs to I_p and its t-th truth-table bit equals b, so these outputs are exactly the new membership vector. This is a uniform exact update for the explicit candidate-list representation; it does not give poly(s,N) cost when M is the full family of size-s circuits.

label: S0016
statement:
statement: Near-linear deterministic range avoidance for subcritical circuit size. Let n tend to infinity, N=2^n, and let s=s(n)=o(n/log(n+2)). Consider ordered fan-in-two circuits on n named inputs with constants 0,1, at most s gates over a fixed finite basis of g>=1 binary operations, and one output wire. There is a deterministic algorithm that outputs an N-bit truth table not computed by any such circuit in time N^{1+o(1)} and polynomial space in N. Proof: Set W=n+s+2. By the circuit-description count, the number K of descriptions is at most (s+1)W(gW^2)^s=2^{o(n)}, since log K=O(log(s+1)+log W+s(log g+2log W))=o(n). Enumerate each valid description and its truth table, retaining this explicit list (or rescanning it); apply the prefix-halving procedure, which uses O(NK) bit inspections and outputs a string outside the list. Enumeration and evaluation add at most K*poly(N,n,s)=N^{1+o(1)} time because K=2^{o(n)} and poly(n,s)=N^{o(1)}. The stored list and counters use at most K*N+poly(N) bits, which is N^{1+o(1)} and hence polynomial in N. The output is outside the size-s circuit image by the prefix-halving invariant. This does not establish the CJSW uniform refuter hypothesis at its larger circuit-size threshold, so G0001 remains open.
evidence: Derived from the already verified description-count bound (claim:10a2c5f610ef) and recorded finite-list prefix-halving lemma S0011; no new finite computation is asserted.

statement:
statement: Lemma (range avoidance for a polynomial list). Fix a constant a. For each N, let L be a list of K<N^a strings of length N. Suppose a uniform procedure returns any requested list entry in poly(N) time. Then a uniform deterministic algorithm outputs y absent from L in poly(N) time and O(N+log(K+1)) extra space. Proof: Start with the empty prefix p. For each position j, count the entries matching p followed by 0 and by 1. These counts sum to the number q matching p, so choose an extension matched by at most q/2 entries. Induction gives at most K/2^j matches after j positions. At j=N this is less than 1, hence zero, so p is absent from L. There are N scans of K entries, each entry retrieved in poly(N) time; the counters and prefix use O(N+log(K+1)) space. This proves a deterministic refuter for polynomial-size, uniformly random-accessible lists only.
evidence: The induction proves the output avoids every list entry, including when entries repeat. The polynomial runtime follows from K<N^a and the stated random-access enumeration bound. This does not establish that the size-s circuit image has such a list for the full CJSW parameter range, so it does not close G0001.

statement: statement: Finite-family exhaustive selector lemma. Let T be a Boolean truth table of length N, let C_s be a finite family of circuit encodings with |C_s| <= 2^{b(s)}, and let V(T,C) be a deterministic verifier that decides whether tt(C^A)=T in time at most v(N,s) for every C in C_s. If some C in C_s satisfies V(T,C)=1, lexicographic exhaustive search returns a satisfying C in at most 2^{b(s)} verifier calls and time at most 2^{b(s)}v(N,s) plus encoding overhead. Proof: enumerate C_s in lexicographic order, run V on each encoding, and return the first accepting encoding. Finiteness and the assumed existence of an accepting encoding imply termination and correctness. Scope: this gives no QE* resource bound unless 2^{b(s)}v(N,s) fits it, and establishes no reduction or P-versus-NP consequence.

structure.evidence: Direct finite enumeration argument; each verifier call is bounded by v(N,s), there are at most |C_s| <= 2^{b(s)} encodings, and existence of a valid witness guarantees an accepting encoding.
structure.gap: No witness family, verifier cost, or parameter regime has been shown to make this exhaustive selector fit the QE* obligation; OBL-QE-W remains open.

statement: Interval-window DP lemma as stated in lemma (correctness by induction on i; state bound from the window and the completed-sum range). Reading B (V unrelated to v) is excluded: the completed-sum range is then unbounded.

structure.lemma: Reading A. Let n, k, D, B, V, T be integers, D, B >= 1, V >= 0, 1 <= k <= n. Let C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, where for each bottom gate j there is a start a_j in {0..n-k} with W_ji = 0 outside [a_j, a_j+k-1], |W_ji| <= B, |v_j| <= V, at most D gates share a start, and m <= Dn. Then the exact count #C is computed by a left-to-right DP whose layer-i state is (completed sum in [-Vm, Vm], tuple of partial sums of the at most Dk active gates, each in [-Bk, Bk]). Layer size is at most (2Bk+1)^(Dk) (2Vm+1), total time O(n D k (2Bk+1)^(Dk) (2Vm+1)) arithmetic operations. If D k log2(2Bk+1) <= n/2 and V <= n^O(1), time is 2^(n/2) poly(n).

statement: Induction on the position i along pi, identical to S0001 with 'active gates' replaced by 'open gates' (those with s_j <= i < e_j). Correctness: each gate's indicator is decided at position e_j, when its partial sum is complete. The state bound uses |partial sum| <= B|supp_j| <= Bn and the cut bound nu(pi). Subsumes S0001 as the special case with nu <= Dk.

structure.lemma: Ordering version (generalises S0001). Let pi be an ordering of the n variables. For each bottom gate j let s_j(pi) and e_j(pi) be the first and last positions of supp(W_j) in pi, and let nu(pi) = max_i #{j : s_j <= i < e_j}, the maximum number of gates whose support spans a cut. Then #C is computed by a DP along pi whose layer-i state is (completed sum in [-Vm, Vm], tuple of partial sums of the open gates, each in [-B n, B n]). Layer size is at most (2Bn+1)^(nu(pi)) (2Vm+1), so the time is poly(n, m, V) (2Bn+1)^(nu(pi)). Interval supports of window k with at most D gates per start give nu <= Dk, which recovers S0001 with the sharper partial-sum range 2Bk+1 in place of 2Bn+1.

label: S0055
statement: LEMMA-C1 (disjoint-support subclass, exact counting). Let f(x) = [sum_{j=1}^m v_j [w_j . x_{S_j} >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, where the supports S_j are pairwise disjoint integer sets, |S_j| = k_j, w_j, t_j, v_j, T integers, V = sum_j |v_j|. Then #f = 2^{n - sum_j k_j} * sum over b in {0,1}^m with sum_j v_j b_j >= T of prod_j N_j(b_j), where N_j(b) = #{y in {0,1}^{S_j} : [w_j . y >= t_j] = b}. Proof: the blocks are disjoint, so the indicator variables [w_j . x_{S_j} >= t_j] are independent over uniform x; the free variables outside the union of supports contribute 2^{n - sum k_j}. Running-time algorithm: a DP over j with state s in [-V, V] (partial sum of v_j b_j), computing N_j by enumerating 2^{k_j} points; time O(sum_j 2^{k_j} k_j + m (2V+1) + n). Hence for k_j <= c log n and V <= poly(n), #f is computed in poly(n) time, versus 2^n for brute force. Exact-check: physalis_code_run cm-766064d60a724398 (400 random instances, n in [3,10], m <= 4, k_j <= 3, 0 mismatches vs brute force on the same instances); EXPLORATORY evidence only, not thr2_evaluate.

structure.gap: Scope limit: disjoint supports give sum_j k_j <= n, so m <= n / min k_j. The O1 target has m = n^1.5 bottom gates (alpha = 1.5), so this subclass cannot be a speed-up at the target size; it does not close O1, O2-bounded-fan-in with overlapping supports, or G0001-G0004. The top gate is decided by the DP over states, so no undecided-gate count is involved. Not an obligation closure: no obligation id is closed; intended only as the base case of O2 (few distinct bottom gates / disjoint support). To count as a speed-up claim this must be run through thr2_evaluate(sharp_sat) on the same instances with a secret seed.

statement: LEMMA-C2 (bounded-overlap conditioning, exact). Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [w_j . x_{S_j} >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n with arbitrary integer supports S_j. Let occ(i) = #{j : i in S_j}, R = {i : occ(i) >= 2}, P_j = {i in S_j : occ(i) = 1}, free = #{i : occ(i) = 0}. Then #f = 2^{free} * sum over a in {0,1}^R of sum over b in {0,1}^m with sum_j v_j b_j >= T of prod_j N_j^a(b_j), where N_j^a(b) = #{y in {0,1}^{P_j} : [w_j . z = ... >= t_j] = b} with z the vector on S_j equal to a on S_j cap R and y on P_j. Proof: for fixed a, the indicator of block j is a function of y_{P_j} only; the sets P_j are pairwise disjoint, so the block indicators are independent under uniform y; summing over b with the threshold condition gives the formula, and summing over a and multiplying by 2^free gives #f. Running time: O(2^{|R|} (sum_j k_j 2^{|P_j|} + m (2V+1))) with V = sum_j |v_j|. Hence #f is computed faster than 2^n by a factor 2^{delta n} whenever |R| + max_j |P_j| <= (1-delta) n (up to poly factors).

label: S0060
statement: LEMMA-HUB (restricted class, exact counting). Setting: n variables; hub set R with |R| = k; the other variables are partitioned into disjoint blocks P_1..P_G. Every bottom gate j has support(W_j) contained in R union P_g(j) for one block g(j); J_g = {j : g(j) = g}. Weights v_j are integers with V = sum_j |v_j| bounded by a polynomial in n. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} = sum over h in {0,1}^k of sum over s >= T of (D_{1,h} * ... * D_{G,h})(s), where D_{g,h}(s) = #{y in {0,1}^{P_g} : sum_{j in J_g} v_j [W_j.(h,y) >= t_j] = s} and * is convolution of integer distributions. PROOF: fix h. The outcomes of the gates in J_g depend only on y_g, and the blocks use disjoint variables, so the block sums are independent over the product set {0,1}^{P_1} x ... x {0,1}^{P_G}; the number of product points with total sum >= T is the convolution formula. RUNNING TIME: computing D_{g,h} takes 2^{|P_g|} evaluations of the gates in J_g, each O(n); the convolutions over the range [-V, V] cost O(G V^2). Total 2^k (sum_g 2^{|P_g|} n m + G V^2) <= poly(n, m, V) * 2^{k + max_g |P_g|}. So if k + max_g |P_g| <= (1 - delta) n and V <= poly(n), #SAT is computed in time poly(n) * 2^{(1-delta) n}.

structure.lemma: Few-distinct-rows subclass (O2). Let n>=1, B>=1, and let W in Z^{m x n} have all entries in [-B,B] and at most r distinct rows, with distinct row set F = {F_1..F_r} (F_f in Z^n), row map sigma: [m] -> [r], thresholds t in Z^m, weights v in Z^m, T in Z. Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n. Then #SAT(f) = sum over s in S of c(s) g(s), where S = {(F_f.x)_f : x in {0,1}^n}, c(s) = #{x : (F_f.x)_f = s}, g(s) = [sum_j v_j [s_{sigma(j)} >= t_j] >= T]. The DP over coordinates i = 1..n (c_{i+1}(s) = c_i(s) + c_i(s - F_{.,i+1})) computes c exactly, since the value vector after i coordinates depends only on x_1..x_i. Every coordinate of s lies in [-Bn, Bn], so |S| <= (2Bn+1)^r. Time: O((nr + m)(2Bn+1)^r) arithmetic operations, times a log factor for hashing. Hence for fixed r and B the count is poly(n, m). Corollary: if r*log2(2Bn+1) <= n/2 the time is 2^(n/2) * poly(n,m), a saving over brute force 2^n * m on this subclass.

label: S0004
statement: statement: For every n≥0, d≥0, and multilinear Q(x)=Σ_{U⊆[n], |U|≤d} c_U x_U over Z, all coefficients c_S and the Boolean-cube sum Σ_a Q(a) can be recovered from the evaluations Q(1_T,0_[n]\T) for |T|≤d. Specifically, c_S=Σ_{T⊆S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|}Q(1_T,0_[n]\T), and Σ_a Q(a)=Σ_{|S|≤d}2^{n-|S|}c_S. Therefore, given evaluation access to Q, the cube sum is computable using at most Σ_{j=0}^d binom(n,j) evaluations and O(3^d binom(n,d)) arithmetic operations (or O(d 2^d binom(n,d)) with straightforward subset accumulation), hence polynomially many evaluations and operations for fixed d. Proof: For each T, Q(1_T,0)=Σ_{U⊆T, |U|≤d}c_U. Möbius inversion on the subset lattice yields the displayed coefficient formula for each |S|≤d. The earlier monomial counting identity gives the cube sum. All queried T have size at most d. This is an exact procedure for bounded-degree multilinear representatives; it asserts no bounded-degree guarantee for general CNF indicators and no ordinary-PIT reduction.

statement: LEMMA (bounded-window DP for MAJ o MAJ): For MAJ o MAJ circuits where each bottom THR gate reads a window of at most k consecutive variables (k = o(n)), the exact count of satisfying assignments can be computed in time 2^{k}·poly(n,m,S) where S = Σ|v_j|, using a DP that maintains the last k−1 variable bits and the running top sum. Proof: states per level ≤ 2^{k−1}·(2S+1); recursion on each variable adds at most 2 transitions; total operations O(n·2^{k}·poly(...)). This yields 2^{o(n)} for any k = o(n), thus shrinking the gap for the bounded-window subclass of G0002.

label: S0007
statement: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (addresses G0001; closure not claimed, pending independent review). Setting: f(x) = [sum_j v_j [sum_{i in S_j} w_{ji} x_i >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, with |S_j| <= k, each variable in at most D supports S_j, m gates, V = max |v_j|. Claim: #f can be computed exactly in time poly(n, m, V) * 2^{n - n/(Dk+1)}. Proof: fix an order of variables; let A_p be the set of variables at positions <= p that lie in some S_j containing a variable at a position > p. Each gate touching A_p contains a suffix variable, so |A_p| <= min(p, Dk(n-p)), and max_p min(p, a(n-p)) = n - n/(a+1) for a = Dk. Dynamic program over p: state = assignment to A_p, value = polynomial in z whose exponent is the sum of v_j over gates already decided. A gate with last position p is determined by the state at step p, since its earlier variables lie in A_{p-1}. Exactness is by induction on p. Time: sum_p 2^{|A_p|} * (2mV+1) * m * 2^k. Scope: all instances with fan-in <= k and max variable degree <= D; weights and thresholds arbitrary. Consequence: for m = n^alpha, alpha < 2, fixed k, D = C n^{alpha-1}, the saving is 2^{Omega(n^{2-alpha})}, superpolynomial, so 2^n / n^{omega(1)} for that subclass. Evidence: cm-7f058b7dae1d4e23 (60 random instances, n in {8,10,12,14}, k in {2,3}; 0 brute mismatches, 0 frontier-bound violations). The exponent itself is not measured; it is a bound.

structure.gap: G0001 remains OPEN for the general class. label: S0010
statement: LEMMA-DIR (repair of S0002 for G0001). Setting: n >= 1, B >= 1, D >= 1. Directions a_1..a_D in Z^n with |a_{d,i}| <= B. Gates j = 1..m, each with direction d(j), threshold t_j in Z, weight v_j in Z. Threshold T in Z. Let N(F) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [a_{d(j)} . x >= t_j] >= T}. CLAIM: N(F) is computed exactly in O(n (2Bn+1)^D (D+m)) arithmetic operations on integers of O(n + log(m B)) bits. PROOF: Let Y(x) = (a_1.x, ..., a_D.x) in Z^D and N_y = #{x : Y(x) = y}. Then N(F) = sum over y of N_y [g(y) >= T], where g(y) = sum_j v_j [y_{d(j)} >= t_j]. Let N^(i)_y count the prefixes x_1..x_i with partial sums y. Recursion: N^(i)_y = N^(i-1)_y + N^(i-1)_{y - c_i}, where c_i = (a_{1,i}, ..., a_{D,i}), because x_i in {0,1}. N^(0) is the point mass at 0. The support of N^(i) lies in the box [-iB, iB]^D, which has at most (2iB+1)^D <= (2Bn+1)^D points. Each step costs at most (2Bn+1)^D D operations. Evaluating g at each of these points costs O(m) naively. The total is therefore O(n (2Bn+1)^D (D+m)). COROLLARY (the subclass): if D <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bn+1), then (2Bn+1)^D <= 2^{(1-delta) n}, so the running time is 2^{(1-delta) n} times n^{O(1)}, and this holds for every m = poly(n), including m = n^alpha for any alpha > 1. For B = poly(n), the condition reads D <= (1-delta') n / log n. The subclass is defined by few distinct weight vectors, not by disjoint supports, so it allows overlapping supports and m > n. SCOPE: the subclass only. It does not cover D = Theta(n) distinct directions, and it is not a general #SAT algorithm.

structure.gap: G0001 is closed for the stated subclass only (few distinct directions D <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bn+1), any m = poly(n)). Honest caveat: LEMMA-DIR is the standard DP over distinct weight vectors, so a reviewer may judge it trivial, which would mean it does not count as progress under the owner's criterion. statement: CLAIMED: Setting: W integer m x n, t and v integer vectors, T integer, all entries bounded by M, rank_Q(W) = r. Claim: the count #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly in time (2nM+1)^r times (n+m) times r times poly(log(nM)) by a dynamic program. Proof: pick r linearly independent rows B_1..B_r of W and columns S with B_S (r x r) nonsingular; Delta = det(B_S) != 0 and |Delta| <= r^(r/2) M^r. Each row satisfies W_j = c_j B with c_j = W_j|_S B_S^{-1}, so a_j = Delta c_j = W_j|_S adj(B_S) is an integer vector. Let z(x) = Bx in Z^r. Then W_j.x = c_j.z(x), so W_j.x >= t_j iff a_j.z(x) >= Delta t_j (flip the inequality if Delta < 0). The DP processes variables 1..n; its state is the partial sum z_p = sum_{i<=p} x_i B_{.,i} with a multiplicity. Every coordinate of z_p has absolute value <= nM, so there are at most (2nM+1)^r states. At the end each state's top value is computed from the gates and the counts with value >= T are summed. Consequence: if r <= n / (4 log2(2nM+1)) and M <= n^O(1), the running time is 2^(n/4) times poly(n,m), which is 2^n / n^omega(1). Scope: only low-rank W (rank r with r log n = O(n)); random W has rank n and is not covered. Evidence: cm-9d2f09f8562c4e75 (exploratory: 300 random low-rank instances, 0 mismatches; max states 392 at rank 2, n=32; 5092 at rank 3, n=32). Needs independent review: the DP correctness, the state bound, and whether this discharges G0001 as recorded.

label: S0017
statement: LEMMA-WIN (window / bandwidth DP, ALGORITHM). Setting: C(x) = sum_{j=1}^m v_j [w_j . x_{I_j} >= t_j], integer v_j, t_j, w_j, where each bottom gate has support in a window I_j = [a_j, a_j + L_j - 1] of length L_j <= L (x in {0,1}^n, n >= 1). Let S = sum_j |v_j|. Claim: #{x : C(x) >= T} is computed exactly in time O(2^L (2S+1) (n + m L)). PROOF. Process bits x_0, ..., x_{n-1} in order. State after reading x_0..x_i: (mask, s), where mask = (x_{i-L+1}, ..., x_i) (padded with 0 for indices < 0) and s = sum of v_j over gates with end e_j = a_j + L_j - 1 <= i whose threshold event holds. Invariant: for a gate with e_j = i, its window [a_j, e_j] has length L_j <= L, so [a_j, e_j] is contained in [i-L+1, i] and its event is a function of mask alone; hence the transition (mask, s) -> (mask', s') with mask' = ((mask << 1) | b) mod 2^L and s' = s + sum of v_j over gates with e_j = i+1 that fire is well defined. Gates are evaluated at their end step, so the DP state carries everything needed: its value at step i is the number of prefixes with that (mask, s). Summing counts over states with s >= T at step n-1 gives the exact count (each full x is one path). Cost: at most 2^L states per step times 2S+1 sum values; each gate is evaluated once per state (cost L_j) and transitions cost O(1) per gate evaluation after precomputing. Total O(n 2^L (2S+1)) plus O(m L 2^L (2S+1)) for gate evaluations, which is O(2^L (2S+1)(n + mL)). COROLLARY. Let s(n) = omega(log n) and L = n - s(n). For the subclass of size m = n^alpha with V = max|v_j| constant (so S <= m V = poly(n)) and span(support of each bottom gate) <= L, the count runs in 2^{n - s(n)} poly(n) = 2^n / n^{omega(1)} time, since 2^{s(n)} = n^{omega(1)}. SCOPE: (i) exact #SAT only, not CAPP; (ii) subclass only: random integer bottom gates have full support (span n-1) with high probability, so the subclass excludes generic instances; (iii) no lower bound transfer is claimed. Evidence for correctness: cm-5c396888cfee4f4a (440 random window instances, n in {6,8,10,12}, 0 mismatches against brute force). Repairs still needed: the generic class (G0007 / G0002), and a proof that the window subclass is not trivial relative to the owner's size target.

statement: ALG-FEWDIR (CLAIMED, scope: THR o THR circuits C(x) = [sum_j v_j [<W_j,x> >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, where all bottom weight vectors W_j in Z^n take at most D distinct values d_1..d_D, and |entries| <= B. Every bottom gate equals [s_{g(j)}(x) >= t_j] for its direction index g(j), so C(x) is a function F(s(x)) with F(s) = [sum_j v_j [s_{g(j)} >= t_j] >= T]. (ii) Dynamic programming: after processing variables x_1..x_i, let N_i(s) = #{(x_1..x_i) : s(x_1..x_i)=s}. Then N_0 = {0:1} and N_{i} is obtained from N_{i-1} by adding 0 or d_{1,i},...,d_{D,i} to each state, which is exact by induction. (iii) #C = sum_{s} N_n(s) F(s). Total O(n (2nB+1)^D (D + m)). Consequence: for D <= c log n and B <= n^k, the time is 2^{O(log^2 n)} * poly(n), hence 2^n / n^{omega(1)} for this subclass. For general m = n^alpha the number of distinct directions can be m, and the bound becomes 2^{Omega(n^{c})}. It does NOT close G0001 or G0007. The result is a standard counting argument, not new; its use is as an O2 subclass theorem.

label: S0032
statement: LEMMA-WIN (subclass: interval supports of length <= L in a fixed order). Setting: f(x) = [sum_j v_j [sum_k w_{j,k} x_{a_j+k} >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, m gates, gate j has support I_j = [a_j, a_j+l_j-1] with l_j <= L, integer weights |w| <= B, |v_j| <= V. PROOF: left-to-right DP. State after position i = (last L-1 bits of x_1..x_i, partial sum s in [-mV, mV]) with a count. At position i, for each state and each new bit b, the window (last L-1 bits, b) contains x_{a_j..i} for every gate j with I_j ending at i (length l_j <= L). Evaluate e_j = [w_j . window >= t_j], add v_j e_j to s, and keep the last L-1 bits. Each assignment x corresponds to exactly one DP path, and each gate's value depends only on x restricted to I_j, which is in the window when the gate is processed, so the final sum over states with s >= T is exactly #f. TIME: n positions x 2^{L-1} keys x (2mV+1) sums x 2 bits x (gates ending here, <= m) x L work = O(n m^2 L V 2^L) arithmetic. For L = (1-delta) n and m, V, B = poly(n) this is 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n) = 2^n / n^{omega(1)}; for L = O(log n) it is polynomial. SCOPE: interval supports in one fixed order only; not general THR o THR. STATUS: CLAIMED, not reviewed. Risk: the reviewer may judge it the standard bandwidth/path-decomposition DP, which would not count as progress under the owner's criterion.

structure.lemma: SUBCLASS DP (exact, proved). Let C = THR o THR with n Boolean inputs, m bottom gates [W_j.x >= t_j], integer weights 0 <= W_j,i <= B, top weights v_j and threshold T. Suppose the m weight vectors take at most c distinct values (as vectors, indexed by inv(j)). Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed by the layered DP over states s in [0, Bn]^c (s_d = W_d . x_{<i} after i variables) in time O(n * m * min(2^n, (Bn+1)^c)) arithmetic operations. Proof: after reading x_0..x_{i-1} define s(x_{<i}) in [0,Bn]^c. Each bottom gate value [W_j.x >= t_j] is a function of s_{inv(j)} at the end, and the step x_i -> s + b*W_{.,i} is a deterministic map on states. So the map x -> s(x) is a function from {0,1}^n to states that commutes with each step; the count of x with s(x)=s equals the DP count (induction on i). C(x) depends only on s(x) at i=n, so #C = sum over final states s satisfying the top predicate of the DP count. Each layer has at most min(2^i, (Bn+1)^c) states.

label: S0050
statement: REPAIR-S (candidate, CLAIMED). Setting: C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, integer W, t, v, T. Split variables into A and B with |A| = a, |B| = b = n - a. For x_A, let u_j(x_A) = sum_{i in A} W_ji x_i, and let lo_j = sum_{i in B} min(W_ji, 0), hi_j = sum_{i in B} max(W_ji, 0). Let c_j(x_A) = clip(t_j - u_j(x_A), lo_j, hi_j + 1) and c(x_A) = (c_j). (a) EXACT IDENTITY: #C = sum over distinct vectors c of |{x_A : c(x_A) = c}| * R(c), where R(c) = #{x_B : sum_j v_j [W^B_j.x_B >= c_j] >= T}. Proof: bottom gate j fires iff W^B_j.x_B >= t_j - u_j. Since W^B_j.x_B lies in [lo_j, hi_j], replacing t_j - u_j by its clip to [lo_j, hi_j+1] leaves the predicate unchanged for every x_B: if t_j - u_j < lo_j both sides are always true, if t_j - u_j > hi_j both are always false, and otherwise the clip is the identity. So the fire pattern depends only on c(x_A). (b) K-BOUND: let K = number of distinct c(x_A). Then K <= prod_j min(N_j, hi_j - lo_j + 2), where N_j = number of distinct values u_j(x_A) <= 2^{|S_j cap A|}, and S_j is the support of W_j. Proof: c_j is a function of u_j alone, so c(x_A) lies in the product of the images of the c_j; the image of c_j has at most N_j elements and lies in the integer interval [lo_j, hi_j+1]. Hence K <= prod_j min(N_j, hi_j - lo_j + 2) <= 2^{sigma(A)} with sigma(A) = sum_j min(|S_j cap A|, L_j), L_j = ceil(log2(hi_j - lo_j + 2)). (c) TIME: the algorithm (enumerate x_A, group by c, compute R(c) by enumerating x_B) runs in poly(n,m) * (2^a + 2^{sigma(A)+b}). COROLLARY (a subclass, stated exactly): let max |W_ji| <= Bw and L = ceil(log2(n Bw + 2)). If for some B of size delta*n, sum_j min(|S_j minus B|, L) <= (1 - 2 delta) n, then with a = (1-delta) n, #SAT of C is computed in poly(n,m) * 2^{(1-delta) n} time. Scope: this is a repair of the refuted lemma (the old bound K_clip * 2^{n/2} is replaced by the per-gate bound, which is not bounded by 2^{n/2}); it does NOT close G0001 or G0007 for the general class; the regime m*L <= (1-2 delta) n is already covered by LEMMA-DIR; the new content is the case where most gates live on a delta*n core B.

label: S0055
statement: BANDWIDTH WINDOW DP (subclass, exact, O2). Let C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, with integer W_{j,k} >= 0, integer t_j, integer v_j >= 0, V = sum_j v_j, and S_j = supp(W_j). Bandwidth b: for every bottom gate j, max S_j - min S_j <= b. Let first_j = min S_j and last_j = max S_j. CLAIM: #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly with O((V+1) 2^b poly(n,m)) operations. PROOF. Read x_0,...,x_{n-1} in order. After reading x_0..x_{i-1}, the state is (u, sigma): u = sum of v_j over gates with last_j < i and value 1; sigma_j = sum over k in S_j, k < i, of W_{j,k} x_k for each gate with first_j < i <= last_j (active); sigma_j = 0 for gates with first_j >= i. Keep counts N_i(u, sigma) of prefixes. SUFFICIENCY: finished gates are already fixed in u; each active gate's final value is [sigma_j + sum over k in S_j, k >= i of W_{j,k} x_k >= t_j], which depends only on sigma_j and the suffix. So the number of completions with C = 1 depends only on (u, sigma), and the layer-to-layer transition is exact by induction; at i = n, C = [u >= T]. WINDOW: for an active gate, last_j >= i and last_j - first_j <= b give first_j >= i - b, so sigma_j is a function of x_{i-b}..x_{i-1}. Hence sigma takes at most 2^b values and each layer has at most (V+1) 2^b states. CONSEQUENCE: for b <= (1-delta) n the count takes 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n, m) time (V poly-bounded). NON-VACUITY: for every alpha the class contains circuits of size n^alpha (supports inside windows of length n/2, many distinct gates available), so this is a proved running time for a subclass of size n^alpha. Weights W are not restricted in size; only the number of distinct sigma values matters.

statement: PROOF. Order variables 0..n-1. Let i be the step after x_i is assigned. Define pi_i = (x_k for k in [i-w+2, i]) (at most w-1 bits) and A_i = A_0 + sum over gates j with max S_j <= i of v_j g_j(x), where A_0 = sum of v_j over constant gates (S_j empty) that are true. Transition: a gate j with max S_j = i has S_j contained in [i-w+1, i], and pi_{i-1} covers [i-w+1, i-1] together with x_i, so g_j is determined by (pi_{i-1}, x_i). Every gate finalized at a step i' > i has min S_j >= i'-w+1 >= i+2-w, so its variables are kept in pi_i. Hence the successor of state (pi_{i-1}, A_{i-1}) under x_i depends only on that state and x_i, and the number of extensions of a state equals the number of x-prefixes mapping to it. By induction the DP's accumulated count per state equals the number of prefixes x_0..x_i with that state, and N(C) = sum of counts over final states with A_{n-1} >= T. STATE BOUND: |pi_i| <= 2^(w-1). Each v_j enters A at most once, so A_i lies in [-R, R] (since A_0 is a subset sum of the v_j) and takes at most 2R+1 values. Hence states <= 2^(w-1)(2R+1). Per step, each state branches twice, and evaluating the gates finalized at step i costs O(w) each; summing gives the stated operation count. SCOPE: the proof needs every bottom gate to have span <= w-1. Random THR o THR with full supports (span ~ n) are NOT in this subclass for w < n; so the result is a subclass result only. It does not reach n^alpha-size general THR o THR for alpha > 1 without a bandwidth or pathwidth bound on the instance.

structure.lemma: BANDWIDTH-DP. Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean variables with m bottom gates g_j(x) = [sum_{k in S_j} c_{jk} x_k >= t_j], where every support S_j lies in an interval of length at most w-1 (max S_j - min S_j <= w-1), |c_{jk}| <= B, integer top weights v_j, R = sum_j |v_j|, top threshold T. Then N(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T} is computed exactly by a dynamic program over variables 0..n-1 whose states are (window pattern, partial top sum), with at most 2^(w-1)(2R+1) states per step, in O(2^(w-1)(2R+1)(n + m w)) operations. For w <= (1-delta)n and R <= poly(n), this gives 2^((1-delta)n) poly(n,m) time for this subclass (the second alternative of obligation O1).
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Order variables 0..n-1. Let i be the step after x_i is assigned. Define pi_i = (x_k for k in [i-w+2, i]) (at most w-1 bits) and A_i = A_0 + sum over gates j with max S_j <= i of v_j g_j(x), where A_0 = sum of v_j over constant gates (S_j empty) that are true. Transition: a gate j with max S_j = i has S_j contained in [i-w+1, i], and pi_{i-1} covers [i-w+1, i-1] together with x_i, so g_j is determined by (pi_{i-1}, x_i). Every gate finalized at a step i' > i has min S_j >= i'-w+1 >= i+2-w, so its variables are kept in pi_i. Hence the successor of state (pi_{i-1}, A_{i-1}) under x_i depends only on that state and x_i, and the number of extensions of a state equals the number of x-prefixes mapping to it. By induction the DP's accumulated count per state equals the number of prefixes x_0..x_i with that state, and N(C) = sum of counts over final states with A_{n-1} >= T. STATE BOUND: |pi_i| <= 2^(w-1). Each v_j enters A at most once, so A_i lies in [-R, R] (since A_0 is a subset sum of the v_j) and takes at most 2R+1 values. Hence states <= 2^(w-1)(2R+1). Per step, each state branches twice, and evaluating the gates finalized at step i costs O(w) each; summing gives the stated operation count. SCOPE: the proof needs every bottom gate to have span <= w-1. Random THR o THR with full supports (span ~ n) are NOT in this subclass for w < n; so the result is a subclass result only. It does not reach n^alpha-size general THR o THR for alpha > 1 without a bandwidth or pathwidth bound on the instance.

statement: PROOF. Read x_0, ..., x_{n-1} in order. After reading x_0..x_{k-1} define the window sigma_k = (x_{k-w+1}, ..., x_{k-1}) (indices < 0 read as 0; 2^(w-1) possibilities) and the partial top sum P_k = sum over j with max S_j < k of v_j g_j(x). Each gate with max S_j = k has S_j inside [k-w+1, k], so g_j(x) is a function of (sigma_k, x_k): the transition P_{k+1} = P_k + sum_{j: max S_j = k} v_j g_j(sigma_k, x_k), sigma_{k+1} = last w-1 bits of (sigma_k, x_k) is well defined. Induction on k: the number of completions of a prefix that give top sum >= T depends only on (sigma_k, P_k), since later gates read only the window and later variables. Hence the DP over keys (sigma, P) with counts is exact. |P_k| <= R, so at most 2^(w-1)(2R+1) keys per step, and each step costs O(keys * (2 + m w)). Final answer: sum of counts over keys with P_n >= T. COROLLARY: if w <= (1-delta) n and R <= poly(n), time is 2^((1-delta) n) poly(n, m) on this subclass. Scope: the subclass requires every bottom support to lie in a window of length (1-delta) n under a fixed variable order; generic random supports of size Theta(n) fall outside it.

label: S0081
statement: S-BANDWIDTH: Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with m bottom gates g_j(x)=[sum_{k in S_j} c_jk x_k >= t_j], where each support S_j is an interval with max S_j - min S_j <= w-1, |c_jk| <= B, integer top weights v_j, R = sum_j |v_j|, top threshold T. Then N(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T} is computed exactly by a DP over variables 0..n-1 whose state after step k is (the last min(k+1, w-1) bits of x, partial top sum s in [-R,R]). The number of states is at most 2^(w-1)(2R+1) and the total time is O(2^(w-1)(2R+1)(n + m w)). Proof: a gate with max S_j = k is evaluated at step k from the window bits, which cover S_j because its width is at most w-1 back from k. A future gate with max S_j = k' > k has min S_j >= k'-w+1 >= k-w+2, so it reads only positions inside the window; the window and partial sum are therefore a sufficient statistic. Consequence: for w <= (1-delta)n and R <= poly(n) (e.g. m = n^alpha, |v_j| <= poly(n)), N(C) is computed in 2^((1-delta)n) poly(n) time. Scope: interval-support subclass only. General overlapping supports (G0001, G0007) are untouched. label: S0093
statement: CLAIM S0011 (ALGORITHM, window subclass). Setting: C = THR o THR on x_0..x_{n-1}, bottom gates g_j(x) = [sum_{i in S_j} c_{j,i} x_i >= t_j] with integer c, t; top weights v_j integer, R = sum_j |v_j|, top threshold T; N(C) = #{x : sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T}. Window hypothesis: S_j subset of [a_j, a_j + w - 1] for all j, with w <= n. PROOF. Process k = 0..n-1. Let Close_k = {j : max S_j = k}. Before reading x_k the DP state is (h, s): h = the last min(k, w-1) bits x_{k-w+1..k-1} (a tuple, at most 2^(w-1) values) and s = sum over gates already closed of v_j g_j in [-R, R] (2R+1 values), with a count of assignments reaching that state. Reading x_k gives the bit window (h, x_k) which covers [k-w+1, k], hence contains S_j for every j in Close_k (since min S_j >= a_j >= k-w+1 for these j, because max S_j = k and S_j lies in an interval of length w). So each gate in Close_k is evaluated exactly, s is updated, and the oldest bit is dropped. Each x is counted in exactly one state path, so the final count of states with s >= T equals N(C). Work: at most 2 * 2^(w-1) * (2R+1) states per step, and evaluating Close_k costs O(|Close_k| w) per state, summed over k gives O(2^(w-1) (2R+1) (n + m w)) bit operations and integer additions (gate sums use the given integer c, t). CONSEQUENCE: for the subclass with window width w = (1-delta) n, m = n^alpha gates and R = poly(n) (weights |v_j| poly-bounded), N(C) is computed in 2^((1-delta) n) poly(n) time. Scope: supports need not be disjoint; each variable may lie in many gates. The subclass is windowed-support (bandwidth-type), not bounded fan-in or bounded width in the CNF sense. OPEN: (i) general supports (w = n) give no saving, so G0001 for the general class and the pathwidth step (G0002) remain open; (ii) the tail term for k > n - w in the write-up; (iii) this closes G0001 only as stated literally (a subclass of size n^alpha with leaves / time <= 2^((1-delta)n)); whether a reviewer counts it as non-trivial is for the reviewer to judge. Evidence: cm-d6a1802f593c4b5f (300 random window instances, n in 3..9, m in 1..6, 0 mismatches vs brute force, max states 268 within bound 2^(w-1)(2R+1)).

label: S0094
statement: CLAIMED ALGORITHM (top fan-in <= 2 subclass): for integer W (m x n, arbitrary m and entries), t, v with |supp v| <= 2, and T, count #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computable in O(2^{n/2} n log(2^{n/2})) arithmetic operations. Proof: pad supp v to two indices with zero-weight dummy gates; for each pattern b in {0,1}^2 with v.b >= T, the conditions g_j(x)=b_j become coordinatewise dominance P_b(x_B) >= Q_b(x_A) in Z^2 for the split x=(x_A,x_B) with |x_A|=floor(n/2) (P_b = +/-W_J.x_B, Q_b = t-W_J.x_A or W_J.x_A-t+1); each pattern count is a 2-D dominance count done by sorting and a Fenwick sweep; patterns are disjoint so the answer is the sum. Exact check: cm-6b6e6034b4cb44d9 (120 instances, 0 mismatches vs brute force, n in {6,8,10,12} plus scale checks at 14 and 16). Scope: top fan-in <= 2 only. Not claimed: general unbounded top fan-in (O1), any transfer to E^NP lower bounds (hardness of the subclass not shown), k-constant fan-in extension (needs k-dim dominance counting, not proved here). Timings are exploration only.

label: S0096
statement: CLAIMED ALGORITHM (O2 subclass: constant top fan-in k, extends S0094): for integer W (m x n), t, v with |supp v| <= k, k a constant, and T, the count #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computable in 2^{n/2} * O(log^{k-1}(2^{n/2})) * 2^k * poly(n) time. Proof: pad supp v to exactly k indices with zero-weight dummy gates. Split x=(x_A,x_B) with |x_A| = floor(n/2). For each pattern b in {0,1}^k with v.b >= T, the events g_j(x)=b_j become coordinatewise conditions P_b(x_B) >= Q_b(x_A) in Z^k, where P_b = +/-W_J.x_B and Q_b = t_J - W_J.x_A (b_j=1) or W_J.x_A - t_J + 1 (b_j=0). The patterns partition {0,1}^n, so the count is the sum over b of the number of pairs (x_A, x_B) with P_b(x_B) >= Q_b(x_A). For fixed b this is an offline k-dimensional orthogonal dominance count between N_B = 2^{ceil(n/2)} points and N_A = 2^{floor(n/2)} queries, done with a k-dimensional range tree in O(N log^{k-1} N) time. Exact check: cm-dbaba1a1eca64057 (180 instances, n in 6..10, fan-in 0..5, 0 mismatches vs brute force). Scope: constant k only. structure.lemma: LEMMA-R2K (subclass R(k,B): each variable read by at most 2 bottom gates, each bottom gate reads at most k variables, bottom weights |W| <= B, top weights |v| <= V, integer thresholds). Let G be the multigraph on the non-constant bottom gates with one edge per variable read by two gates and one pendant half-edge per variable read by one gate. Let pw be its pathwidth. Then #SAT is computed exactly by a variable-order DP whose state is the tuple of partial sums of open gates plus the top accumulator, in time poly(n,m) * (2Bk+1)^(pw+1) * (2Vm+1). Proof: take a path decomposition of G with width pw and the layout of gates it induces (vertex separation <= pw); process variables ordered by their larger endpoint. A gate is open after a prefix iff it has a processed edge and an unprocessed edge, so at most pw+1 gates are open. An open partial sum is a sum of at most k weights bounded by B, so it takes at most 2Bk+1 values; the top accumulator takes at most 2Vm+1 values. Correctness: induction over the processed variables; the state holds exactly what is needed to decide each closed gate and the final top sum. Cited premise (from memory, SOURCE-CHECK before any review): Kneis, Molle, Richter, Rossmanith (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2009) give pw(G) <= e/5.769 + O(log n) for a graph with e edges. With e <= n this gives time 2^((log2(2Bk+1)/5.769 + o(1)) n) * poly; for B = 1, k = 2 the exponent is about 0.403 n.

structure.lemma: Cut-crossing DP (lane B, repair of G0002 on a narrower subclass). Let C = (W, t, v, T) be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with m bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], integer weights |W_ji| <= B, integer top weights v_j with V = sum_j v_j, and K(C) = max over cuts i in {0..n} of #{ j : min supp(W_j) < i <= max supp(W_j) } (the number of bottom gates whose support crosses cut i). Then #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x) = 1} can be computed exactly in time O(n * m * K * (2Bn+1)^K * (V+1)) arithmetic operations. PROOF: process variables x_0, ..., x_{n-1} in order. After the first i variables, the state is (s, tau): s = (s_j) for the gates j open at cut i, where s_j = sum_{l < i} W_jl x_l, and tau = sum of v_j over gates already closed (max supp(W_j) < i) and satisfied. Each s_j lies in [-Bn, Bn], so there are at most (2Bn+1)^K vectors s, and tau in {0..V}. The count of prefixes with a given state is a sum over the previous state and the bit x_i, and the update of each s_j is additive, so the transition is exact; a gate j is decided at its last support index, when its final sum is known. Summing counts over states with tau >= T gives the answer. Correctness on finite data: dp_count agrees with brute force (see evidence).

Not a closure of G0001: the subclass is banded (every variable meets few gates), and generic THR o THR instances have K = Theta(m).

label: S0106
statement: Windowed cut DP (refinement of S0100, does NOT close G0001/G0002). Let C = (W,t,v,T) be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j.x >= t_j], |W_ji| <= B, integer top weights v_j. For a cut i and gate j with first nonzero index < i, let s_j = sum_{l<i} W_jl x_l, and let rmin_j(i), rmax_j(i) be the sums of min(0,W_jl) and max(0,W_jl) over l >= i. Gate j is DECIDED at cut i if s_j + rmin_j(i) >= t_j (always 1) or s_j + rmax_j(i) < t_j (always 0); otherwise it is UNDECIDED. Let U = max over cuts i of the number of undecided started gates. Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly by the DP whose state is (s restricted to undecided gates, tau), where tau = sum of v_j over decided-satisfied gates, in O(n m (2Bn+1)^U (sum_j |v_j| + 1)) arithmetic operations. PROOF: (i) Invariant: after x_0..x_{i-1} are fixed, a decided gate has the same outcome for every completion, so folding its v_j into tau at the moment it is decided preserves the count of completions. (ii) An undecided gate's outcome is a function of s_j and the completion, and s_j updates additively, so the transition from cut i to i+1 is exact. (iii) Each s_j lies in [-Bn, Bn], giving at most (2Bn+1)^U x (sum|v|+1) states per cut. (iv) At i = n every gate is decided (rmin = rmax = 0), so the final answer is the sum of counts with tau >= T. Since U <= K (the cut-crossing number), this refines S0100.

label: S0109
statement: S-RANK-r (CLAIMED, not reviewed by this session): Let C be a THR o THR circuit with m bottom gates [W_j.x >= t_j], integer weights |W_ji| <= B, rational thresholds t_j, integer top weights v_j and top threshold T, and r = rank_Q(W). Then #SAT(C) can be computed exactly with O(n (2Bn+1)^r poly(m,n,r)) arithmetic operations. Proof: pick r independent rows Bm of W. Each row satisfies W_j = c_j Bm with exact rational c_j, so W_j.x = c_j.s(x) with s(x) = Bm x in Z^r. Run a layered DP over variables 1..n. After prefix p the state s_p has coordinates in [-Bp, Bp], so there are at most (2Bn+1)^r states. Keep the number of prefixes reaching each state. Gate values depend only on the final state, so sum the counts of states whose top sum is >= T. Scope: rank r of W, integer weights bounded by B, any poly(m). This subsumes the distinct-direction DP S0010. It does not close G0001 or G0002. The 2^((1-delta)n) bound needs r log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta)n, i.e. r = o(n / log n) for bounded B. Evidence: cm-a8ea3bacdc574c44 (72 instances, 0 mismatches), cm-3b8036f363ce479a (54 instances, exact rational gate values, 0 mismatches). Void run cm-955c3739d5c44569 excluded.

label: S0120
statement:
Lemma (s-shared subclass #SAT). Let C be a THR∘THR circuit with n inputs, m bottom gates, integer weights and thresholds, and top weights v_j with V = Σ|v_j|. Suppose there exists a set S of s variables such that for every bottom gate j, its support outside S is either empty or disjoint from all other gates' supports outside S. Let F be the set of free variables (outside all bottom-gate supports). Then #SAT(C) can be computed exactly in time O(2^s · m · n · V).

Proof.
1. Enumerate all a ∈ {0,1}^S (2^s assignments). For each a:
2. For gate j, let base_j = Σ_{k∈S} W_{j,k} a_k. Its private variables P_j are disjoint across j. Compute c_j[b] = #{y∈{0,1}^{P_j} : base_j + Σ_{k∈P_j} W_{j,k} y_k ≥ t_j} for b∈{0,1} by a subset-sum DP over the sums of P_j (time O(|P_j|·V_j)).
3. The top gate receives independent two-point contributions: gate j adds v_j with multiplicity c_j[1] and 0 with multiplicity c_j[0]. Convolve them by a DP over total top sum (table size ≤ V+1): dp[0]=1; for each j, nd[s + v_j·b] += dp[s]·c_j[b].
4. Count for this a is Σ_{s≥T} dp[s]. Multiply by 2^{|F|}.
5. Sum over all a.

Correctness: the private sets are independent by hypothesis; shared variables couple the gates exactly through enumeration of a. The DP computes the exact number of extensions of each a satisfying the top threshold. Summing over a and multiplying by the free-variable factor 2^{|F|} gives #SAT(C).

Running time: 2^s · (m·n·V) = O(2^s · poly(m,n,V)).

Exhaustive check on 20 random instances (n∈{8,10,12}, m∈{4,6,8}, s∈{0..5}, B∈{3,5,20}): cm-b5d9ef4c88e14bb6 — all exact counts match brute force. This is a non-trivial exact algorithm for a stated subclass.

label: S0127
statement: CLAIMED. SUBCLASS RESULT (O2, low-rank weights). Setting: W in Z^{m x n} of rank r over Q; B in Z^{r x n} = r linearly independent rows of W with |B_ik| <= beta; every row W_j = C_j B with C_j in Q^r. Input t, v in Z^m, T in Z. Claim: N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed EXACTLY in O((beta n + 1)^r (n + m r)) arithmetic operations on integers. Proof. (1) Exactness: s(x) = Bx in Z^r and W_j.x = C_j.s(x). So N = sum over sigma in Z^r of H(sigma) [g(sigma) >= T], where H(sigma) = #{x : Bx = sigma} and g(sigma) = sum_j v_j [C_j.sigma >= t_j]. (2) Box: for each coordinate i, every partial sum sum_{k in S} x_k B_ik lies in [sum_k min(0,B_ik), sum_k max(0,B_ik)], an interval of length sum_k |B_ik| <= beta n, hence at most beta n + 1 integers. So all partial prefix sums lie in a box Q with at most (beta n + 1)^r points. (3) DP: H_0 = indicator of 0; H_l(sigma) = H_{l-1}(sigma) + H_{l-1}(sigma - B_{.,l}) (x_l = 0 or 1). Each of the n steps touches only points of Q, at O(r) per point. (4) Final sum over Q of H_n(sigma) [g(sigma) >= T], with C_j cleared to integer denominators, O(m r) per point. Total O((beta n+1)^r (n + m r)) operations. (5) Consequence: if r <= (1-delta) n / log2(beta n + 1), then (beta n+1)^r <= 2^{(1-delta) n}, so N is computed in 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n, m) time for ANY m = poly(n) and any top-gate data (v, T, t). With beta = poly(n) this covers r = Theta(n / log n). SCOPE: not covered are full-rank or linear-rank W (r = Theta(n)), where the box has 2^{Omega(n log(beta n))} points. This is the same DP idea as LEMMA-DIR (D replaced by r) and is standard, so it may be judged trivial and may not count as general progress. It is a subclass O2 result only; G0001 stays open for the general class.

label: S0131
statement: BANDWIDTH DP for the subclass B_k of THR o THR circuits. Circuit C(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T], g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], with V = sum_j |v_j|. Hypothesis: there is a variable order 1..n such that every bottom support S_j = {a : W_j[a] != 0} lies in an interval of length <= k. Claim: #SAT(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x) = 1} is computed exactly in O(2^k (n + mk)(2V+1)) arithmetic operations. Proof. For 0 <= i <= n let F_i = {u <= i : u and some b > i lie in a common support}. Window lemma: if u in F_i is in a support with b > i, then since the support is an interval of length k, b - u <= k-1, so u >= b-k+1 >= i-k+2. Hence F_i is contained in [i-k+2, i] and |F_i| <= k-1. Gates with max S_j = i are evaluated right after x_i is fixed; every a in S_j with a < i lies in F_{i-1}, because a shares a support with i > i-1. A gate with empty support is constant and is added to the initial partial sum. Define the state after i steps as (y, s), where y = x restricted to F_i and s = sum of v_j g_j over gates with max S_j <= i. Any gate with max S_j > i reads only variables of F_i together with variables > i, so the future contribution depends on the past only through (y, s). Hence N_i(y, s) = #{x_1..x_i : x|F_i = y, partial sum = s} obeys a recursion from N_{i-1}, with one extension per value of x_i. The number of states is at most 2^(k-1)(2V+1). Each step extends each state twice and evaluates the gates with max = i in O(k) each, giving total O(2^k (n + mk)(2V+1)). The final count is the sum of N_n(., s) over s with s >= T. Induction on i gives correctness. Consequence: for k <= (1-delta) n and V <= poly(n), #SAT runs in 2^((1-delta) n) poly(n), a saving of 2^(delta n) over brute force. Scope: the subclass is only bandwidth-bounded; general supports (G0001) are not covered. Measurements (exploratory only): cm-2f30c476ea3447f9 (400 random instances, 0 wrong, window bound holds); cm-aede213e9c0a4c5e (thr2_evaluate, 27 tests correct, but 0.006-0.009x brute-force speed at n <= 14).

structure.gap: Open: (i) the subclass needs a bandwidth order; (ii) general THR o THR with overlapping supports of size Theta(n) (G0001, G0007) is not covered; (iii) the DP is slower than brute force at n <= 14, so the saving is only asymptotic, not measured.

label: S0132
statement: LEMMA (frontier DP, reduction of G0002 to a width bound). Let C = top THR_{T}(v) over m bottom gates g_j = [W_j . x >= t_j] with integer weights |W_{j,i}| <= B, supports |S_j| <= k, integer top weights |v_j| <= V. Fix any variable order pi = (x_{pi(1)}, ..., x_{pi(n)}). Let w(pi) = max over prefixes P of the number of bottom gates whose support meets P and is not contained in P (active gates). Then #C is computed exactly by a DP over the prefixes whose state is (a) the vector of partial sums sum_{i in S_j cap P} W_{j,i} x_i for the active gates, each in [-Bk, Bk], and (b) the scalar sum of v_j g_j over completed gates, in [-Vm, Vm]. Number of states <= (2Bk+1)^{w(pi)} (2Vm+1), and the transition cost is poly(m, n). Hence #C is computed in time poly(n, m, V) * (2Bk+1)^{w(pi)}. Proof: each state is the full information about the prefix that the future depends on: the future value of g_j for an active gate depends only on its partial sum, and completed gates enter only through the top sum. Exactness is by induction on the prefix. CONSEQUENCE: if w(pi) <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bk+1) for some order, then #C is in 2^{(1-delta) n} poly time. SCOPE: bounded weights B, bounded support k, any m = poly(n). This is a reduction of G0002 to a frontier bound, not a proof of the bound. Gap: a proved bound w(pi) <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bk+1) for a subclass of size n^alpha, which is G0002/G0007. Measured on the family c=3 occurrences per variable, k=4, m=3n/4, B=2 (cm-29b0966debef4ea4): greedy width/n is 0.35 to 0.44; the lemma's threshold is 1/log2(17) = 0.245, so the lemma does NOT yield a saving on this family.

label: S0136
statement: BANDED LEMMA. Let C = top THR_T(v) over m bottom gates g_j = [sum_{i in S_j} W_{j,i} x_i >= t_j]. Each support S_j = {a_j, ..., a_j+k-1} is an interval of length k, |W_{j,i}| <= B, |t_j| <= Bk, |v_j| <= V, and at most D gates share the same start a_j. Then #C = #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x)=1} is computed exactly by a DP over variables 0..n-1 in order. After prefix P = {0..p-1}, the active gates are those with min S_j < p <= max S_j. Their starts lie in [p-k+1, p-1], so there are at most (k-1)D active gates. DP state = (partial sums s_j = sum over S_j cap P of W_{j,i} x_i for active j, each in [-Bk, Bk]; sum of v_j g_j over completed gates, in [-Vm, Vm]). This state is all the future depends on, so exactness follows by induction on p. Number of states <= (2Bk+1)^{(k-1)D} (2Vm+1); time poly(n, m, V) (2Bk+1)^{(k-1)D}. statement: S-BW-TM-1 (CLAIMED, needs independent review). STATEMENT: Let C be a THR o THR circuit on variables x_1..x_n with bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], integer W_j, and top gate [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T] with integer v_j. Let V = sum_j |v_j|. Fix a variable order. Let I_j = [a_j, b_j] be the smallest interval containing supp(W_j), and let w = max_j (b_j - a_j + 1) (the order's bandwidth of C). Then #SAT(C) is computed exactly in O(2^w (V+1) (n + m w)) arithmetic operations. PROOF: Define for i = 0..n the window sigma_i = (x_{i-w+1}, ..., x_i) with x_k := 0 for k < 1, and the partial sum s_i = sum over j with b_j <= i of v_j g_j(x). The DP table D_i maps (sigma, s) to the number of prefixes x_1..x_i with window sigma and partial sum s. Start: D_0 = {(0^w, c0) : 1}, where c0 = sum of v_j over constant gates with the value 1 (gates with empty support, evaluated at 0). Step i -> i+1: for each entry (sigma, s) and bit x in {0,1}, let sigma' = (sigma shifted left, x) truncated to w bits, and s' = s + sum over j with b_j = i+1 of v_j [W_j . sigma'_restricted >= t_j]. CORRECTNESS: a gate j with b_j = i+1 reads only variables in I_j subset of [i+1-w+1, i+1], which are exactly the coordinates of sigma'. So its value is a function of sigma', and the transition is exact. Induction on i gives: D_i(sigma, s) = #{prefixes x_1..x_i : window = sigma, partial sum = s}. Gates with b_j > i are not yet added and read nothing outside the window at their later time, so no information needed later is discarded. Output: sum of D_n(sigma, s) over s >= T. RUNNING TIME: at most 2^w states per s-value, and s ranges over an interval of length at most V+1, so each table has at most 2^w (V+1) entries. Per step, each entry is processed for two bits, and the gates with b_j = i+1 are evaluated once each in O(w). Total O(n 2^w (V+1) + 2^w (V+1) m w). COROLLARY: if every bottom gate has span at most w = n - k and V <= poly(n), #SAT(C) is computed in 2^(n-k) poly(n) time, so with k = omega(log n) this is 2^n / n^{omega(1)} for this subclass. SCOPE / LIMITS: (1) the order is an input; computing a minimum-bandwidth order is itself hard, so the running time counts only the DP given the order. (2) The subclass is the bounded-bandwidth one; it does not cover generic THR o THR, where every span is n (measured: speedup 0.006, cm-d1e0e3d177544ee2). (3) Not measured by thr2_evaluate: its families are full-span, so this lemma is a proof, not a speed claim. OPEN: overlapping supports with bounded pathwidth of the incidence graph (G0002 beyond bandwidth), and whether a subclass with m = n^alpha bottom gates and bandwidth n - omega(log n) is rich enough for the O1 target (G0001/G0007).
