statement: PROOF. (1) Primal graph: x and y are neighbours if they share a support. Each x has at most d(x) <= 6 neighbours (3 supports, each with at most 2 others). (2) Ordering DP: fix an order of the variables; for the prefix up to position p let F_p = {x at position <= p with a neighbour at position > p}. Process variables in order, keep the state (assignment of F_p, partial sum s in 0..V_tot), evaluate gate j when its last variable is introduced (all its variables are then in the state), and forget x when all its gates are evaluated. Correctness is by induction; the number of states is at most 2^{|F_p|} (V_tot+1) and each step costs poly(m). Total time 2^{max_p B_p} poly, where B_p = #{x : pos(x) <= p and some neighbour at position > p} >= |F_p|. (3) Expectation for a uniformly random order: for p = tn with p >= 6 and d = d(x) <= 6, P(x and all d neighbours at position <= p) = prod_{i=0..d} (p-i)/(n-i) >= ((p-d)/n)^(d+1) >= (t - 6/n)^7, so E[B_p] <= n(t - t^7) + 42 <= 0.62 n + 42, since max over t of t - t^7 is at t = 7^(-1/6) with value about 0.6197. (Positions p < 6 contribute at most 6.) (4) Concentration: a transposition of two positions changes at most 14 indicators (the two moved variables and their at most 12 neighbours), so B_p is 14-Lipschitz under transpositions. A concentration inequality for random permutations (Maurey 1979, constant to be source-checked) gives Pr[B_p >= 0.63 n] <= exp(-Omega(n)) for each p; a union bound over p <= n gives an order with max_p B_p <= 0.63 n for large n. Hence time 2^{0.63 n} poly. SCOPE: this subclass only, not general THR o THR. EVIDENCE: exploration run cm-dd159f73f1ee4c79 (0 mismatches vs brute force, frontier about n/2 at n <= 14) is consistent but is not a proof; the new measurement run in this session checks the frontier ratio at n = 100, 200, 400. CAVEATS: (a) bounded-occurrence pathwidth counting is standard and a reviewer may judge it folklore, which would mean it does not count as progress; (b) step (4) relies on a cited concentration inequality, which must be source-checked; (c) the earlier subcubic pathwidth bound n/6 for the incidence graph (Fomin-Hoie / Kneis et al.) is an alternative route and is NOT used, since its source is unverified here. CONSEQUENCE: closes G0002 only for this subclass, with exponent 0.63 < 1; G0001 for the general class remains open.

statement: THEOREM (subclass SPLIT(b)). Let n >= 8, b >= 0 fixed, W integer m x n, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, with |W_ji| <= n^b and m <= n/(4(b+1) log2 n). Then #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computed exactly in time poly(n,m) * 2^(3n/4+1). PROOF. Let k = floor(n/2), s = n-k, x = (p,q) with p in {0,1}^k, q in {0,1}^s, and split W_j = (A_j, B_j). Let lo_j = sum_i min(0,B_ji) and hi_j = sum_i max(0,B_ji), so B_j.q lies in the integer interval [lo_j, hi_j] for every q. Let tau_j(p) = t_j - A_j.p and clip_j(tau) = min(max(tau, lo_j), hi_j+1). Step 1: for every integer tau and every q, [B_j.q >= tau] = [B_j.q >= clip_j(tau)]. If tau <= lo_j both sides are 1; if tau > hi_j both sides are 0; otherwise clip_j(tau) = tau. Step 2: put kappa(p) = (clip_j(tau_j(p)))_j. Then f(p,q) = F(kappa(p), q), where F(K,q) = [sum_j v_j [B_j.q >= K_j] >= T]. Step 3: with mu(K) = #{p : kappa(p) = K} and N(K) = #{q : F(K,q) = 1}, we have #f = sum over realised K of mu(K) N(K). Step 4 (algorithm): enumerate the 2^k prefixes and compute kappa(p) in O(mk) arithmetic time, tallying mu in a hash table; for each realised K enumerate the 2^s suffixes and evaluate F in O(ms) time; output the sum from Step 3. Correctness follows from Steps 1-3. Step 5 (time): the first phase costs O(2^k m k). The second phase costs |K*| * 2^s * O(ms), where K* is the set of realised kappa vectors. Each K_j lies in {lo_j, ..., hi_j+1}, a set of size hi_j - lo_j + 2 = sum_i |B_ji| + 2 <= s n^b + 2 <= n^(b+1) (using n >= 8). So |K*| <= n^((b+1)m) = 2^(m(b+1)log2 n) <= 2^(n/4) by the bound on m. Hence the total time is poly(n,m) (2^(n/2) + 2^(n/4) 2^(n/2+1)) = poly(n,m) 2^(3n/4+1). QED. SCOPE. Correctness holds for every integer input; the running-time bound uses the subclass only. The subclass has m = o(n) bottom gates, far below the n^alpha (alpha > 1) size regime of the Chen-Tal-Wang transfer, so no circuit lower bound follows from this speed-up. OBSTACLE for linear m: the bound |K*| <= n^((b+1)m) needs m log n <= n/4; for m = Theta(n) the product of window sizes exceeds 2^(n/2). NEXT ENRICHMENT (not proved, the next step to try): count the distinct residual functions F(K, .) rather than the distinct K; if that count is 2^(o(n)) for linear m, the same algorithm extends. Status: CLAIMED, not reviewed by another session. Measurement: thr2_evaluate sharp_sat with the code in the next experiment.

statement: WINDOW LEMMA (exact-window interval class C(n,k,D)). Input: W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji|<=B, v_j in [-V,V], thresholds t_j, T. Class: there is an unknown column order pi* such that for each row j the nonzero columns of W_j are EXACTLY a block of k consecutive positions of pi*, and at most D rows share the same block. Claims: (a) Every ordering sigma under which every row's support is consecutive (C1P) satisfies nu(sigma) <= Dk, where nu(sigma) = max_p #{j : p in span_sigma(j)}. Proof: span = support = an interval of length k; the intervals of length k containing p are exactly k (left end in [p-k+1,p]); each exact interval has at most D rows. (b) A C1P ordering is found in time linear in the matrix size by a PQ-tree (Booth-Lueker); pi* is one such ordering. (c) For any ordering sigma, the DP over positions computes #{x: sum_j v_j [W_j.x>=t_j] >= T} exactly (induction on p: a gate is decided at its last support position; state = (sum of v over decided gates, partial sums of open gates)). (d) An open gate's partial sum lies in [-Bk,Bk], so the number of states at p is <= (2Vm+1)(2Bk+1)^{nu(sigma)} <= (2Vm+1)(2Bk+1)^{Dk}. With m <= Dn and k <= c n/(D log2 n), c<1: Dk log2(2Bk+1) = (c+o(1)) n, so the count is computed in time poly(n) 2^{(c+o(1)) n} on C(n,k,D). This is a speed-up over 2^n for windows of length Theta(n/log n). Gaps: (i) exact windows only (zero entries inside a window are excluded); (ii) the multiplicity D is essential, since without it nu can be m; (iii) (c) and (d) need an independent review; (e) the claim is not a speed-up for general THR o THR.

statement: Bandwidth DP for THR o THR #SAT. Setting: variables 1..n in a FIXED order that is part of the input. Bottom gate j has integer weights W_j with support S_j (nonempty), last(j) = max S_j, window L_j = max S_j - min S_j + 1. Top gate: integer v_j, integer T, f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. Let l = max_j L_j and V = sum_j |v_j|. Claim: #f = #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computed exactly in time O(n^2 m 2^(l-1) (2V+1)). Proof: process i = 1..n. Frontier F_i = {u <= i : u in S_j for some j with last(j) > i}. Claim |F_i| <= l-1. If u in F_i via gate j, then u >= min S_j = last(j) - L_j + 1 >= i+2-l, so F_i lies in [i+2-l, i], a set of size at most l-1. DP state after step i: (assignment to F_i, partial top sum P over gates with last(j) <= i), with the count of prefixes x_1..x_i producing it. Transition by choosing x_{i+1}: a gate with last(j) = i+1 reads only coordinates u in S_j with u <= i (which lie in F_i, since last(j) > i) and u = i+1, so its value is determined by the state and x_{i+1}; add its weighted value to P; keep F_{i+1}. Final answer = sum of counts over states with P >= T. Number of states at most 2^(l-1) (2V+1), since P lies in [-V, V]. Correctness follows by induction on i.

Bottom gate j has integer weights W_j with support S_j (nonempty), last(j) = max S_j, window L_j = max S_j - min S_j + 1. Top gate: integer v_j, integer T, f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. label: S0158
statement: SUB-V2 (exact algorithm and running time, for all integer THR o THR). Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] with m gates over n variables, all |W_ji|, |t_j|, |v_j| <= B. Let V2 = union of supp(j) over gates with |supp(j)| >= 2, and l = |V2|. Let V1 = (union of supp(j) over unary gates) minus V2, k = |V1|, V0 = [n] minus (V1 union V2). Algorithm: (a) for each unary gate on i in V1 set a_i += v_j (b1_j - b0_j), c += v_j b0_j, where b0_j = [0 >= t_j], b1_j = [W_ji >= t_j]; (b) let A be the remaining gates; for each y in {0,1}^{V2} compute S(y) = sum over A of v_j [W_j.y >= t_j] (A-gates have support inside V2, see the identity); (c) compute the distribution of sum_i a_i z_i over z in {0,1}^{V1} by an integer DP of range at most 4nmB+1; (d) output 2^{|V0|} * sum_y #{z : sum a_i z_i >= T - c - S(y)}. Correctness: the identity of S0007 (SURVIVED_REVIEW). Time: O(2^l (mn + n^2 m B)) arithmetic operations plus O(nmB) precomputation. Consequence (SUBCLASS C_delta): instances with |V2| <= (1-delta) n, any m = poly(n), weights bounded by poly(n), are counted in time 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n,m,B) with NO variable ordering needed (V2 is computed directly). Exact for all instances: general time 2^{|V2|} poly <= 2^n poly. Scope: this is a constant-base saving on a subclass, not 2^n / n^{omega(1)}, and it does not close G0001 in general (the general class can have V2 = [n]). Open for the next step: a subclass where |V2| is small but m is n^alpha and the supports are unbounded in count, or an enrichment where the 2^{l} enumeration is replaced by a DP over the V2 supports (pathwidth of the V2 gate hypergraph, G0002). Authored by R1075; not reviewed by its author.

label: S0192
statement: S0040 (CLAIMED, unreviewed). Setting: f(x) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [<w_{idx(j)}, x> >= t_j] >= T} for m bottom gates whose weight vectors take at most d distinct values w^(1..d) in Z^n with |w^(k)_i| <= B; t_j, v_j, T arbitrary integers. Claim: f is computed exactly in O(n (2Bn+1)^d (m d + 1)) arithmetic operations. Proof: DP over prefixes. For level i let z_k = <w^(k)_{<=i}, x_{<=i}> for k = 1..d; the state is z in Z^d. Since |z_k| <= B i <= Bn, there are at most (2Bn+1)^d states per level. The transition from level i-1 to i adds b * w^(k)_i to each z_k for b in {0,1}, so the count table at level i is a function of the table at level i-1. Each gate value [<w_{idx(j)},x> >= t_j] is a function of the final z alone, so f = sum over final states z with sum_j v_j [z_{idx(j)} >= t_j] >= T of their counts. Correctness is by induction on i. Scope: polynomial time when d is constant and B is polynomial in n. GAP: this does not close G0001. General THR o THR needs d = Theta(m) (the measured thr2 family, cm-c77b7124cbc643ef, has about one form per gate), and the bound is exponential there. It is a standard, self-made subclass bound; it counts as progress only after review with confirms_closure, and it is not progress by itself.

label: S0249
statement: Lemma (signed top weights on disjoint supports). Let W be an integer m×n matrix whose row supports S_1,...,S_m are pairwise disjoint, let t_j,v_j,T be integers, and define c_j = |{y∈{0,1}^{S_j}: Σ_{i∈S_j} W_{ji}y_i ≥ t_j}| and f=n−Σ_j|S_j|. Then the exact number of satisfying inputs is 2^f Σ_{e≥T}[z^e]∏_{j=1}^m((2^{|S_j|}−c_j)+c_j z^{v_j}), where the product is a Laurent polynomial if some v_j<0. It is computable using O(Σ_j 2^{|S_j|}+m(2V+1)) arithmetic operations, where V=Σ_j|v_j|, with DP exponents restricted to [−V,V]. Proof: each row event depends only on its support, so an assignment induces an event pattern b∈{0,1}^m with top sum Σ_jv_jb_j. For each j, exactly c_j assignments on S_j make b_j=1 and exactly 2^{|S_j|}−c_j make b_j=0. Disjointness makes the number realizing pattern b the product of these counts; the f variables outside all supports contribute 2^f. Expanding the Laurent product groups these pattern counts by exponent e=Σ_jv_jb_j, so summing coefficients for e≥T gives the formula. Every partial exponent lies between −V and V, giving at most 2V+1 DP entries per gate; enumerating each support computes c_j in O(2^{|S_j|}) evaluations. This is an exact subclass algorithm; it does not close the overlapping-support obligation.

label: S0252
statement: statement: Component factorization lemma. Let W be an integer m-by-n matrix, with row supports S_j={i:W[j,i] != 0}, integer thresholds t_j, integer top weights v_j, and target T. Form the graph on rows, joining j,k iff S_j intersects S_k. For each connected component C let U_C=union_{j in C} S_j, and let a_C(e) count assignments y in {0,1}^{U_C} for which sum_{j in C} v_j [sum_{i in S_j} W[j,i] y_i >= t_j]=e. Then #SAT of the top threshold equals 2^{n-|union_C U_C|} times sum_{e>=T}[z^e] product_C (sum_e a_C(e) z^e). Proof: different components have disjoint variable unions by the edge definition, so their local assignment choices are independent and multiply; their top scores add, so polynomial multiplication groups assignments by total score. Variables outside all row supports are free, contributing the stated power of two. If every |U_C|<=w, this exact algorithm takes O(sum_C 2^{|U_C|} (|C|+|U_C|) + |C| V) arithmetic operations, where V=sum_j |v_j|, and O(V+1) coefficient storage; exponents lie in [-V,V]. Thus bounded component-union width w=O(log n), polynomial m,V, and polynomial-bit input arithmetic give polynomial bit time. This shrinks the overlap-support gap only for that explicitly bounded-component subclass.

label: S0257
statement:
statement: Component-score dynamic program for bounded incidence components. Let W be an integer m×n matrix, t,v∈Z^m and T∈Z. Define S_j={i:W_{ji}≠0} and partition the bipartite gate-variable incidence graph into connected components (J_a,U_a). For each component define H_a(z)=Σ_{x∈{0,1}^{U_a}} z^{Σ_{j∈J_a}v_j·1[Σ_{i∈U_a}W_{ji}x_i≥t_j]}. Then #SAT is 2^{n-|∪_a U_a|} Σ_{e≥T}[z^e]∏_a H_a(z). If each |U_a|≤b and V=Σ_j|v_j| is polynomially bounded, computation takes O(Σ_a2^{|U_a|}+r(V+1)^2) arithmetic operations and O(V+1) coefficient storage, where r is the number of components. For b=O(log n), m,V polynomial in n, and polynomial input bit lengths, this is polynomial-time in the bit model.
proof: Every gate support lies in one incidence component, and distinct components have disjoint variable sets. Restricting an assignment to U_a determines the outputs of gates J_a, hence their component score. The coefficient of z^q in H_a counts assignments to U_a with score q. By distributivity, the coefficient of z^e in the product counts assignments to all covered variables with total score e, preserving multiplicity. Variables outside the covered union occur in no gate and contribute 2^{n-|∪U_a|}. Summing coefficients for e≥T therefore gives exactly the satisfying assignments. Compute each H_a by enumerating 2^{|U_a|} local assignments. Every score is in [-V,V], so each histogram and partial convolution has O(V+1) entries. Sequential convolution takes O(r(V+1)^2) arithmetic operations and O(V+1) storage. If b=O(log n), then Σ_a2^{|U_a|}≤r2^b is polynomial because r≤m. Intermediate counts are at most 2^n, hence have polynomial bit length; with polynomial bit-length inputs and polynomial m,V, the total bit complexity is polynomial.
evidence: Independent VERIFICATION experiment cm-61fff845705a4341 compared a separately implemented component histogram/convolution algorithm with brute force on 1,200 generated instances (n=0..5, m=0..4; signed entries, thresholds, top weights; zero mismatches). This is finite corroboration only; the proof above establishes the general identity and stated complexity. This lemma concerns a bounded-component subclass and does not close the unrestricted overlapping-support gap.

label: S0258
statement:
statement: Sparse component-score dynamic program for arbitrary binary-encoded top weights. Let W be an integer m-by-n matrix, t,v in Z^m and T in Z. Partition the gate-variable incidence graph into components (J_a,U_a), each with at most b variable vertices. Let P_a be the set of distinct scores s_a(x)=sum_{j in J_a} v_j [sum_{i in U_a} W_{ji}x_i >= t_j] for x in {0,1}^{U_a}, and q_a=|P_a|. Define M_0=1 and let M_a be the number of distinct accumulated scores after processing components 1..a. The exact #SAT count is computed with at most sum_a 2^{|U_a|} + sum_{a=1}^r M_{a-1}q_a score-map operations, times polynomial bit cost, where M_a <= product_{c<=a} q_c; unused variables contribute 2^{n-|union U_a|}. No polynomial bound on sum_j |v_j| is required for this sparse representation.
proof: Enumerate every assignment to U_a and tally its score, obtaining a map from P_a to multiplicities. Initialize a map with score zero and multiplicity one. At each component, form the next map by adding each score in the current map to each score in the component map and multiplying their multiplicities; merge equal resulting scores. Inductively, the map after a components counts assignments to the disjoint union of their variable sets by total score: the induction step follows from the unique decomposition of an assignment into its restrictions to the previous components and the new component. Thus summing multiplicities for scores at least T gives the satisfying assignments on covered variables. Variables outside the union of component variable sets occur in no gate and independently contribute 2^{n-|union U_a|}. Component enumeration uses 2^{|U_a|} assignments, and combining maps uses M_{a-1}q_a pair operations. Each score is a sum of at most m input integers, so its bit length is polynomial in the input bit length. The maps can nevertheless have exponentially many entries, so this establishes an exact output-sensitive algorithm, not a general polynomial-time algorithm.
evidence: General proof by induction on the number of processed incidence components. The finite experiment cm-61fff845705a4341 checked the underlying component factorization independently on 1,200 small signed-weight instances, but did not test sparse-map complexity; it is corroboration only.

statement: statement: Lemma (Exact #SAT by bounded incidence components). Let a threshold-of-threshold instance have Boolean variables x_1,...,x_n, bottom gates g_j(x)=[sum_i W_{ji}x_i >= t_j] for j=1,...,m, integer top weights v_j, and top condition sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T. Form the bipartite incidence graph with variable vertices and gate vertices, joining x_i to g_j exactly when W_{ji} is nonzero. Suppose every connected component containing a gate has at most b variable vertices. Then the exact number of satisfying assignments can be computed in O(2^b (n+m) + m^2 V) arithmetic operations, where V=sum_j |v_j|; variables in no gate are included as isolated components. Proof: For each component C, enumerate all 2^{|X_C|} assignments to its variable set X_C and evaluate its incident bottom gates, producing a histogram h_C(q) counting assignments whose incident gates contribute total q=sum_{j in C} v_j g_j. The graph has no edge between distinct components, so each bottom gate depends only on variables in its own component and the top sum is the sum of the component contributions. statement: statement: Let W be an integer m-by-n matrix with pairwise disjoint row supports S_j, each |S_j| <= c log_2 n for a fixed constant c. The exact number of x in {0,1}^n satisfying sum_j v_j [sum_i W[j,i]x_i >= t_j] >= T is computable in deterministic polynomial time, specifically O(sum_j 2^{|S_j|} + m(V+1)) arithmetic operations. Proof: For each j enumerate the 2^{|S_j|} assignments to S_j and compute c_j, the number satisfying its threshold. Since supports are disjoint, each gate bit is realized by c_j assignments with bit 1 and 2^{|S_j|}-c_j with bit 0; the n-sum_j|S_j| variables outside all supports are free. label: S0291
statement: statement: Lemma (exact #SAT for logarithmic incidence components). Fix constants c,d. Let C be an explicitly represented THR∘THR instance on n Boolean variables with m≤n^d bottom gates. Assume every connected component of its variable/gate incidence graph contains at most c log₂(n+2) variables; all bottom and top integer weights and thresholds have absolute value at most n^d. Then #SAT(C) is computable exactly in polynomial time. Proof: The incidence components partition the variables, and each bottom gate is adjacent only to variables in its own component. For each component i, enumerate its at most 2^{c log₂(n+2)}=(n+2)^c assignments. For each assignment, evaluate its incident bottom gates and record the resulting contribution z to the top weighted sum; aggregate a table A_i[z] counting assignments with contribution z. Each evaluation and table construction takes polynomial time. Since there are at most m gates, each of polynomially bounded weight, every component contribution and every partial sum has absolute value at most m·n^{2d}, a polynomial bound; thus each table has polynomially many possible integer indices. Initialize D_0[0]=1 and iteratively set D_i[t]=Σ_z D_{i−1}[t−z]A_i[z]. By induction, D_i[t] counts exactly the assignments to the first i components whose total top score is t: the induction step partitions those assignments uniquely by their last-component assignment and its contribution z. Therefore #SAT(C)=Σ_{t≥T}D_k[t], where T is the top threshold. There are at most n components and polynomially many score indices, so the convolutions use polynomially many arithmetic operations. Every count is at most 2^n and therefore has at most n+1 bits; exact integer arithmetic is polynomial time. This proves the lemma, including negative weights, empty components, and isolated variables (an isolated variable contributes a two-assignment table at score zero).

statement: statement: Fixed-distinct-predicate #SAT algorithm. Fix constants q,d,e. Let C have n Boolean variables and m<=n^e bottom gates, each equal to one of at most q distinct predicates h_r(x)=[sum_{i=1}^n a_{r,i}x_i >= b_r], with integer |a_{r,i}|,|b_r|<=n^d. The top gate is [sum_{j=1}^m v_j g_j(x)>=T], with integer |v_j|,|T|<=n^e, and each g_j is one of the h_r. Then #SAT(C) is computable exactly in polynomial time for fixed q,d,e. Proof: For prefix length i and score vector s in Z^q, let D_i(s) count assignments to x_1,...,x_i whose rth partial score is s_r. Initialize D_0(0,...,0)=1. For variable i, update D_i(s)=D_{i-1}(s)+D_{i-1}(s-a_i), where a_i=(a_{1,i},...,a_{q,i}); splitting assignments according to x_i=0 or 1 proves this invariant by induction. Every coordinate satisfies |s_r|<=i n^d<=n^{d+1}, so each layer has at most (2n^{d+1}+1)^q states. Counts have at most n+1 bits. At i=n, each score vector determines each h_r by comparison with b_r and thus determines the top predicate. Sum D_n(s) over precisely those vectors where sum_j v_j h_{g_j}(s)>=T. For fixed q,d,e the state count, transition count, and bit complexity are polynomial in the explicit input length. statement: statement: Lemma (exact #SAT for a fixed number of distinct bottom threshold predicates). Fix constants q,d,e. Let C be a THR∘THR circuit on n Boolean variables, with m≤n^e bottom gates. Suppose every bottom gate is one of q predicates h_r(x)=[Σ_{j=1}^n a_{r,j}x_j≥b_r], where all a_{r,j},b_r are integers of absolute value at most n^d. Suppose the top gate is [Σ_{j=1}^m v_j g_j(x)≥T], where each g_j is one of the h_r and |v_j|,|T|≤n^e. Then #SAT(C) is computable exactly in polynomial time for fixed q,d,e. Proof: For 0≤i≤n and s∈Z^q, define D_i(s) to be the number of assignments to x_1,…,x_i whose rth partial sum Σ_{j≤i}a_{r,j}x_j equals s_r for every r. Set D_0(0)=1 and all other D_0(s)=0. For i≥1, write a_i=(a_{1,i},…,a_{q,i}); then D_i(s)=D_{i−1}(s)+D_{i−1}(s−a_i). Indeed, assignments counted by D_i(s) partition into those with x_i=0, whose first i−1 variables have score s, and those with x_i=1, whose first i−1 variables have score s−a_i. Thus the recurrence computes every D_i exactly by induction. Since |a_{r,j}|≤n^d, every reachable coordinate at layer i has absolute value at most i n^d≤n^{d+1}; hence each layer has at most (2n^{d+1}+1)^q reachable score vectors. At layer n, h_r(x) is determined by whether s_r≥b_r. Therefore each final score vector determines every bottom gate output, and hence whether the top threshold accepts. Summing D_n(s) over exactly the accepting score vectors gives #SAT(C). Each count is at most 2^n and has at most n+1 bits. For fixed q,d,e, the number of states and transitions is polynomial in n; evaluating the top threshold and adding the counts also takes polynomial bit time because m≤n^e and the weights and threshold have polynomial magnitude. This proves the claimed exact polynomial-time algorithm for this subclass.

statement: Let W∈Z^{m×n}, thresholds t∈Z^m, top weights v∈Z^m, and T∈Z. Suppose the supports S_j={i:W_{ji}≠0} are pairwise disjoint. Define c_j=|{y∈{0,1}^{S_j}: Σ_{i∈S_j}W_{ji}y_i≥t_j}| and f=n−Σ_j|S_j|. Set L=−Σ_{j:v_j<0}v_j and P(z)=∏_{j=1}^m((2^{|S_j|}−c_j)+c_j z^{v_j+L_j}), where L_j=−v_j if v_j<0 and 0 otherwise. For each gate j the exponent shift is local; instead define Q(z)=∏_j((2^{|S_j|}−c_j)z^{L_j}+c_j z^{L_j+v_j}), with L_j=max(0,−v_j). Then # {x∈{0,1}^n: Σ_j v_j[Σ_iW_{ji}x_i≥t_j]≥T}=2^f Σ_{e≥T+L}[z^e]Q(z), where L=Σ_jL_j. proof: Disjoint supports make the gate truth indicators independent under uniform assignments, and each block has exactly c_j assignments making its gate true and 2^{|S_j|}−c_j making it false. For gate j, a false assignment contributes score 0 and a true assignment contributes v_j. Multiplication of the corresponding two-term polynomials records the number of block assignments by total score after shifting both exponents by L_j=max(0,−v_j); all exponents are nonnegative. Thus Q's coefficient at e counts block assignments with original total score e−L. The f unused variables contribute a factor 2^f, and summing coefficients for e≥T+L gives exactly the required count. Enumerating each block computes c_j in Σ2^{|S_j|} operations; naive multiplication of m polynomials whose total degree is D costs O(mD²) arithmetic operations. This is an exact finite subclass algorithm; it provides no speed-up claim for unrestricted or overlapping supports.

statement: Let C be a THR∘THR circuit on n Boolean variables with m bottom gates, each bottom gate depending on at most k variables. Let U be the union of the bottom-gate supports. There is an exact #SAT algorithm running in O(2^{|U|} poly(n,m)) time, hence O(2^{mk} poly(n,m)); for every fixed δ>0, the subclass mk≤(1−δ)n is countable in O(2^{(1−δ)n} poly(n,m)) time.
proof: Enumerate every assignment a∈{0,1}^U and evaluate each bottom threshold gate and then the top gate on a. Let A be the number of enumerated assignments accepted. Every gate output, and therefore C's output, depends only on variables in U. Thus each accepted assignment a has exactly 2^{n−|U|} extensions to {0,1}^n, all accepted, and each rejected assignment has no accepted extensions. Therefore #SAT(C)=A·2^{n−|U|}. The union bound |U|≤mk gives the stated enumeration time and the subclass bound. Evaluating the circuit per assignment costs polynomial time in its encoding size.

label: S0003
statement: LEMMA (polynomial-time collision selector from an explicit transition table). Let A be a deterministic binary streaming machine with m>=1 states, given by its complete transition table and initial state. Set k=ceil(log2(m))+1. Enumerate the 2^k binary words of length k lexicographically, compute each word's terminal state by k table lookups, and return the first pair of distinct words with equal terminal states. Such a pair exists because 2^k>m and the map from length-k words to the m states cannot be injective. The procedure therefore terminates, returns a valid equal-length collision, and uses O(k*2^k)=O(m log(m+1)) transition lookups and O(k+log m) working bits, apart from storing the input table. This is a polynomial-time selector given the explicit transition table; it does not show that the selected words are generated by a polylogtime-uniform AC0 family.

label: S0010
statement: Lemma (Speed-up via residual-state pruning): Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean inputs with m = ceil(n^alpha) bottom threshold gates. Let L be the set of distinct affine linear forms represented by the bottom gates. If |L| <= r with r <= 2, then there exists a deterministic algorithm A_C that decides the number of satisfying assignments of C in time T_C(n) = 2^{n-(r-1)} * poly(n). Proof: 1. Residual state: For an assignment x define sigma(x) = {(Delta_i, w_i) | i=1..m} where Delta_i = sum_{j in S_i} x_j - t_i is the offset of gate i after fixing the variables that appear in its linear form, and w_i is the weight of that form. Two assignments have the same sigma exactly when every bottom gate's threshold test yields the same outcome. 2. Bounding distinct sigma: Each linear form in L is affine, so for a fixed assignment the offset Delta_i can be <=0 or >0 (two possibilities). Because weights w_i are fixed, sigma is determined solely by the r distinct linear forms. Hence |sigma({0,1}^n)| <= 2^r. 3. Partitioning search space: Group all assignments that share the same sigma. Within a group the values of all bottom gates are already fixed, so the remaining sub-problem depends only on unassigned variables and sigma. The effective branching factor is reduced from 2 per variable to at most 2^{1-(r-1)/n} per variable. 4. Constructive algorithm: Process variables sequentially, maintaining a map M from sigma to current partial count. Initially M{sigma_0}=1. When variable x_k is set to 0 or 1, each entry of M is updated by adding the contribution (at most two new sigma-states per entry). The map never contains more than 2^r entries, each update costs O(1), giving total running time O(2^{n-(r-1)} * poly(n)). For r=2 the algorithm visits at most 2^{n-1} nodes, a factor-2 speed-up over brute force.

structure.lemma: Repair of S0010 (bounded-form DP). Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean inputs with m bottom gates g_j(x) = [w_j.x >= t_j], integer weights |w_{j,i}| <= B, top gate f(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T]. Suppose the bottom weight vectors take at most r distinct values u^(1),...,u^(r), with k(j) the index of gate j's form. Then #SAT(C) = |{x : f(x)=1}| is computed exactly by a deterministic procedure using O(n*r*(2Bn+1)^r + m*(2Bn+1)^r) arithmetic operations. Proof: (1) For a prefix i, define s(i) in Z^r by s_k(i) = sum_{l<=i} u^(k)_l x_l. Then |s_k(i)| <= B*i, so s(i) lies in [-Bi,Bi]^r and has at most (2Bi+1)^r <= (2Bn+1)^r values. (2) Process variables in order x_1,...,x_n, keeping a map M_i from state vectors to the number of prefixes with that state. M_0 = {0 -> 1}. Step i+1 sends each state s to s + bit*u_{.,i+1} for bit in {0,1}, adding counts; this is exact because the contribution of x_{i+1} to each form depends only on bit. Each step touches at most 2|M_i| entries, each of cost O(r). (3) At the end, g_j(x) is a function of s(n)_{k(j)} alone, namely [s_{k(j)} >= t_j]. Hence f(x) is a function of s(n) alone, and sum_x f(x) = sum_{s} M_n(s) * f(s). Evaluating f on each final state costs O(m). (4) Total cost: sum over levels of O(r |M_i|) <= O(n r (2Bn+1)^r), plus O(m (2Bn+1)^r) for final evaluation. Corollary: if r*log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta)n for a fixed delta>0, the running time is poly(n,m) * 2^{(1-delta)n}, a saving of 2^{delta n} over brute force. For constant B this means r = O(n / log n) distinct forms, with m unrestricted (gates may share forms). SCOPE: this covers THR o THR circuits with few distinct bottom forms (many gates allowed). It does NOT cover generic THR o THR with r = m = n^1.5 distinct forms, so it does NOT close G0001 and does not give a speed-up for the generic case.

label: S0024
statement: LEMMA (support-restricted bounded-weight DP; corrects the refuted S0010 by bounding weights and counting only the top support). Let C(x) = [sum_{j in J} v_j [w_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, where J = {j : v_j != 0}, integer weights |w_{j,i}| <= B, integer thresholds, integer T. Let r be the number of DISTINCT vectors among {w_j : j in J}. Then #SAT(C) = |{x : C(x)=1}| is computed exactly by a deterministic procedure in O(n r (2Bn+1)^r + |J| (2Bn+1)^r) arithmetic operations. PROOF: (1) Fix distinct forms F_1..F_r. For prefix length i and form k set s_k(i) = sum_{l<=i} F_{k,l} x_l. Then |s_k(i)| <= B i <= Bn, so s(i) lies in a set of size at most (2Bn+1)^r. (2) Let M_i(s) = #{prefixes x_{1..i} : s(i) = s}. M_0(0)=1. Then M_{i+1}(s) = M_i(s) + M_i(s - F_{.,i+1}) (x_{i+1}=0 keeps s, x_{i+1}=1 adds column i+1); this is exact because the only dependence of s on x_{i+1} is through the column F_{.,i+1}. Each step touches at most 2 |M_i| entries, each of cost O(r). (3) Gate j in J equals [s_{k(j)}(n) >= t_j], a function of the final state only, so C(x) = g(s(n)) for a fixed g evaluable in O(|J|). Hence #SAT = sum_s M_n(s) g(s), at cost O(|J|) per state. (4) Summing: O(n r (2Bn+1)^r) for the DP and O(|J|(2Bn+1)^r) for the final sum. COROLLARY: if r log2(2Bn+1) <= n - omega(log n), the time is 2^n / n^{omega(1)}; if r log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta) n, it is 2^{(1-delta)n} poly(n). For constant B and constant r it is polynomial. SCOPE AND LIMIT: the bound is driven by r over the top support. For generic instances with |J| ~ m ~ n^1.5 and distinct forms, r is of order m and the corollary gives no saving, so G0001 is NOT closed. The lemma is a proved subclass result (bounded weights, few distinct forms in the top support, e.g. bounded top fan-in combined with bounded B). It does not repair the generic gap. It does explain the lab counterexample cm-120b2921bf9842cd: that instance has B = 2^(n-1), so (2Bn+1)^1 is not polynomial and the lemma's hypothesis fails. Code: count_sat submitted to thr2_evaluate (objective sharp_sat); the speed claim is decided by that experiment, not by this lemma.

statement: ALGORITHM (subclass, rank-d bottom layer, bounded weights). Let C be THR o THR with bottom weights |w_jk| <= B, top gate f = [sum_j v_j g_j >= T], rank_Q(W) = d. Then #SAT(C) is computable in time poly(n,m) * d * (2Bn+1)^d. Proof: choose d independent rows B of W; every row w_j = sum_k c_jk w_{B_k} with rational c_jk, so g_j(x) = [c_j . y >= t_j] for y = W_B x in Z^d, and f(x) = F(y). #SAT = sum_y N(y) F(y), where N(y) = #{x : W_B x = y} is computed by the column DP over partial sums (at most (2Bn+1)^d states, O(n d (2Bn+1)^d) time), then F is evaluated on each state at O(m d) cost. If d <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bn+1), the time is poly(n) 2^{(1-delta) n}. Scope: low-rank or bounded-rank bottom layer only; generic m ~ n^1.5 random integer forms have d = n and the bound is vacuous. Does not close G0001. Restates the counting in G0006 as an exact DP with a running-time bound.

statement: CLAIMED. Lemma A (few-top-gate DP, subclass). Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [w_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, integer weights |w_ji| <= B, integers t_j, v_j, T. Let S = {j : v_j != 0}, k = |S|. Then #f = |f^{-1}(1)| is computed exactly in O(mn + n k (2Bn+1)^k) integer operations. Proof: (1) gates with v_j = 0 do not affect f. (2) Process x_1..x_n in order; keep N_i(p) = #{(x_1..x_i): partial sums p_j = sum_{l<=i} w_jl x_l equal p for j in S}. (3) N_0 = {0 -> 1}; N_{i+1}(q) = sum_{b in {0,1}} N_i(q - b w_{.,i+1}). (4) |p_j| <= B i <= Bn, so the table has at most (2Bn+1)^k entries; each step costs O(k) per entry per bit. (5) [w_j.x >= t_j] = [p_j >= t_j] at i = n, so #f = sum_p N_n(p) [sum_{j in S} v_j [p_j >= t_j] >= T]. (6) If k log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta) n the time is poly(n) 2^{(1-delta)n}; if k = O(log n) and B <= n^{O(1)} the time is 2^{O(log^2 n)} <= 2^n / n^{C} for every fixed C at large n. QED. Scope: bounded-weight, few-nonzero-top-weight subclass. Not a speed-up claim on generic instances (k ~ m ~ n^1.5 > n makes the bound vacuous).

statement: PROOF. Process variables x_1..x_n in order. After i variables, the state is the vector p^(i) = (sum_{l<=i} w_{j,l} x_l)_{j=1..k}, which lies in {-Bi,...,Bi}^k, so at most (2Bi+1)^k <= (2Bn+1)^k distinct states occur. Maintain a dictionary from state to the number of prefixes reaching it. Step i+1: each state p with count c spawns p (x_{i+1}=0) and p + w_{.,i+1} (x_{i+1}=1), each with count c. This keeps the multiset of prefix-states exact by induction on i, because the final state depends only on the prefix sums. After n steps every state p gives g_j = [p_j >= t_j] for all j, so the top value is sum_j v_j g_j, and #F = sum over states with top value >= T of their counts. Each step does O(k) work per state, so the total is O(n k (2Bn+1)^k) and space is the same up to the number of states. CORRECTNESS: the count of prefixes per state is preserved, and the final test uses exactly the bottom gates' values since w_j . x = p_j after n steps. COROLLARY: if k <= c log2 n and B is constant, (2Bn+1)^k = 2^{c log2(n) log2(2Bn+1)} = 2^{O(log^2 n)}, so the total time is 2^{O(log^2 n)} poly(n), and the ratio to brute force 2^n is 2^{-(n - O(log^2 n))} = n^{-omega(1)}. SCOPE: class C(c,B) = THR o THR with at most c log2 n bottom gates of nonzero top weight and bottom weights in [-B,B]; no restriction on the number of bottom gates with zero top weight. NOT covered: generic m ~ n^1.5 bottom gates with all top weights nonzero (k = m), where the bound is (2Bn+1)^{n^1.5}, which exceeds 2^n. This does NOT close G0001 and does NOT close G0002, G0004 or G0006. statement: statement_start: LEMMA (layer-sensitive top-support DP). Let f(x) = [sum_{j=1}^m v_j [W_j·x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, with integer W_j[i], t_j, v_j, T and |W_j[i]| <= B. Let J = {j : v_j != 0}, k = |J|. Define D_i(z) as the number of assignments to x_1,...,x_i whose active-form vector (W_j[1..i]·x)_{j in J} equals z. Then D_0(0)=1 and D_i(z)=D_{i-1}(z)+D_{i-1}(z-W_J[:,i]). For each i, D_i has at most min(2^i,(2Bi+1)^k) reachable states. Summing D_n(z) over vectors z for which sum_{j in J} v_j [z_j >= t_j] >= T returns #SAT(f). The algorithm takes O(k*sum_{i=0}^n min(2^i,(2Bi+1)^k) + k*min(2^n,(2Bn+1)^k)) arithmetic operations and O(min(2^n,(2Bn+1)^k)) stored states; counts use at most n+1 bits.

label: S0075
statement: Let C be a THR∘THR circuit with one top threshold gate and bottom threshold gates. Form the variable–gate incidence graph, connecting a variable to each bottom gate on which it depends. Suppose every bottom gate has support contained in one connected component, and each component has at most w variables. Write the top gate as 1[sum_j a_j h_j(x) >= T], with integer weights a_j. For each component H, define its local score distribution D_H(s) as the number of assignments to variables in H whose weighted sum of bottom gates supported in H equals s. Bottom gates of empty support contribute a fixed score c0. Then #SAT(C) equals the sum, over s0+sum_H s_H >= T, of the product_H D_H(s_H), where s0=c0. Proof: each Boolean assignment restricts uniquely to one assignment on each component. Because every nonconstant bottom gate is supported in exactly one component, the top score is c0 plus the sum of the corresponding local scores. Conversely, every tuple of component assignments combines uniquely to a global assignment. Thus grouping global assignments by their component scores yields the stated product-and-sum formula. Computing each D_H by enumerating its at most 2^w assignments costs O(2^w times the number of incident gates) arithmetic operations in total over components. Convolving the distributions over the integer score range [-B,B], where B=sum_j |a_j|, costs O(kB) additions with a rolling dynamic program, where k is the number of components; integer bit lengths are polynomial in the circuit encoding length. Therefore this gives an exact algorithm with time O(2^w poly(L)+kB), where L is circuit encoding length, for this subclass; it is not a sub-2^n bound absent further restrictions on w and B.

statement: ALGORITHM (two active bottom gates, polynomial coefficients). For every n-variable THR∘THR instance with integer bottom weights W, thresholds t, top weights v, and threshold T, suppose at most two indices j have v_j != 0 and |W_{ji}| <= n^2 for every such j and input coordinate i. Exact #SAT is computable in polynomial time. Let J={j:v_j != 0}, k=|J|<=2. At layer i store D_i(z), the number of prefixes x_1,...,x_i whose active weighted-sum vector (sum_{h<=i} W_{jh}x_h)_{j in J} equals z. Initialize D_0(0)=1. For a_i=(W_{ji})_{j in J}, update D_i(z)=D_{i-1}(z)+D_{i-1}(z-a_i), treating absent entries as zero. Inductively, the two terms count disjoint prefixes according as x_i=0 or x_i=1. Each coordinate lies in [-i n^2,i n^2], so each layer has at most (2n^3+1)^2 states, also when k<2. At i=n, gate j outputs [z_j>=t_j]; inactive gates contribute zero to the top sum. Summing D_n(z) over states with sum_{j in J} v_j[z_j>=t_j]>=T gives exactly #SAT. There are n layers, polynomially many states per layer, and counts have at most n+1 bits. Threshold and top-weight arithmetic is polynomial in their input bit lengths, so total bit complexity is polynomial in the instance encoding length. This restricted result gives no general THR∘THR speedup. Diagnostic: it establishes no P!=NP claim and makes no lower-bound claim, so the four barrier and circumvention tests do not apply.

statement: LEMMA (exact count by repeated active columns). Fix n,m≥0 and an integer THR∘THR instance with W∈Z^{m×n}, thresholds t∈Z^m, top weights v∈Z^m and threshold T∈Z. Let J={j:v_j≠0}. Partition input coordinates into r nonempty classes I_1,...,I_r such that the active-column vector (W_{ji})_{j∈J} is constant on each I_a; denote it c_a and let q_a=|I_a|. Then #SAT is the sum, over tuples k_a∈{0,...,q_a} satisfying Σ_{j∈J}v_j·1[Σ_a k_a(c_a)_j≥t_j]≥T, of ∏_a binom(q_a,k_a). proof: For an assignment x, let k_a count its 1-coordinates in I_a. Since columns within I_a have the same active vector c_a, the active weighted sum for gate j is Σ_a k_a(c_a)_j. Thus acceptance depends only on the tuple (k_1,...,k_r). Exactly ∏_a binom(q_a,k_a) assignments realize each tuple, since the classes are disjoint. The tuples partition all assignments, so summing these multiplicities over the accepting tuples gives #SAT. There are at most ∏_a(q_a+1) tuples; computing each tuple’s active sums and acceptance condition costs O((|J|+r)∏_a(q_a+1)). Counts are at most 2^n, hence use at most n+1 bits.

statement:
statement_start: For a THR∘THR circuit whose active bottom-gate columns have at most a fixed r distinct vectors, #SAT is computable in polynomial time.
statement: Let C be an integer THR∘THR circuit on n Boolean inputs. Let J be the set of bottom gates with nonzero top weight. Suppose the input coordinates are partitioned into r nonempty classes I_1,...,I_r such that each column (W_{ji})_{j in J} is constant on each class. Let q_a=|I_a| and let c_a be that column vector. Then #SAT(C) equals the sum over tuples k_a in {0,...,q_a} for which the top gate accepts, of product_a binom(q_a,k_a), where bottom gate j is evaluated at sum_a k_a(c_a)_j. For each fixed r this is computable in polynomial time in the circuit's binary encoding length. Proof: every assignment induces the unique tuple k_a=number of its 1-coordinates in I_a; the active gate sums and hence output depend only on this tuple. Exactly product_a binom(q_a,k_a) assignments induce it, since classes are disjoint. Thus summing multiplicities over accepting tuples counts satisfying assignments exactly once. There are at most product_a(q_a+1) <= (n+1)^r tuples. Each tuple can be evaluated using polynomially many integer additions and comparisons on numbers whose bit lengths are polynomial in the input encoding length; the binomial multiplicities also have at most n+1 bits. Therefore for fixed r the total bit complexity is polynomial. This is an exact algorithm for the fixed-distinct-active-column subclass only.

statement:
statement: Let C be an integer THR∘THR circuit on n Boolean inputs, with active bottom-gate columns partitioned into r nonempty classes I_1,...,I_r such that each active column vector (W_{ji})_{j in J} is constant on a class. Write q_a=|I_a| and let L be the binary encoding length. Then #SAT(C) is computable exactly in 2^{O(r log(1+n/r))} poly(L) bit operations. In particular, any family with r=o(n) admits a 2^{o(n)} poly(L) exact counting algorithm. Proof: for each tuple k_a∈{0,...,q_a}, evaluate each active bottom gate on the sum of its column coordinates weighted by k_a, then the top gate. Add ∏_a binom(q_a,k_a) iff accepted. Every assignment induces exactly one tuple, and each tuple has exactly that many assignments, so the sum is exact. There are ∏_a(q_a+1) tuples. By concavity of log(1+x), this is at most (1+n/r)^r. Each tuple evaluation and multiplicity computation uses polynomially many bit operations in L; all intermediate integer bit lengths are polynomial in L, since weights/thresholds are encoded in L and counts are at most 2^n. Hence time is (1+n/r)^r poly(L)=2^{O(r log(1+n/r))}poly(L). For r=o(n), r log(1+n/r)=o(n), proving the subexponential consequence. This extends the fixed-r lemma without implying a bound for generic instances, where r may equal n.

statement: statement: Let C be an explicitly encoded integer THR∘THR circuit with n inputs and top weights a_j. Form the variable–bottom-gate incidence graph, and let its variable-containing components be H_1,...,H_k, each with at most w variables. Put B=Σ_j|a_j|. Then #SAT(C) is computable in O(k·2^w·poly(L)+k·(B+1)^2·poly(L)) bit operations, where L is the encoding length. Proof: Empty-support bottom gates contribute a fixed score c_0. Each other bottom gate touches variables in exactly one component. For each H_i, enumerate its at most 2^w assignments and tabulate D_i(u), the number with local weighted bottom-gate score u; this costs O(k·2^w·poly(L)). Initialize A_0(c_0)=1. For i=0,...,k−1 update A_{i+1}(s)=Σ_u A_i(s−u)D_{i+1}(u). By induction, A_i(s) counts assignments to the first i components with total score s. The recurrence partitions these assignments by the next component’s local score. Every global assignment has a unique tuple of component assignments, and its top score is c_0 plus their local scores. Thus #SAT(C)=Σ_{s≥T}A_k(s). All reachable scores lie in [−B,B], so direct score-range convolution costs O(k·(B+1)^2) arithmetic operations. Scores and counts have polynomially many bits in L, giving the stated bit bound. Consequently the algorithm is polynomial time if w=O(log L), B=poly(L), and k≤L.

For each H_i, enumerate its at most 2^w assignments and tabulate D_i(u), the number with local weighted bottom-gate score u; this costs O(k·2^w·poly(L)). Initialize A_0(c_0)=1. For i=0,...,k−1 update A_{i+1}(s)=Σ_u A_i(s−u)D_{i+1}(u). By induction, A_i(s) counts assignments to the first i components with total score s. The recurrence partitions these assignments by the next component’s local score. Every global assignment has a unique tuple of component assignments, and its top score is c_0 plus their local scores. Thus #SAT(C)=Σ_{s≥T}A_k(s). All reachable scores lie in [−B,B], so direct score-range convolution costs O(k·(B+1)^2) arithmetic operations. Scores and counts have polynomially many bits in L, giving the stated bit bound. Consequently the algorithm is polynomial time if w=O(log L), B=poly(L), and k≤L.

statement: statement: Let H_1,...,H_k be the variable-containing components of the variable–bottom-gate incidence graph of an integer THR∘THR circuit. Let U_i be the set of distinct weighted top-score contributions attainable by assignments to H_i, and let c_0 be the contribution from empty-support gates. Define R_0={c_0} and R_i={s+u:s in R_{i-1},u in U_i}. Exact #SAT is computable in O(sum_{i=1}^k |R_{i-1}||U_i| poly(L)) bit operations, where L is the circuit encoding length. Proof: Enumerate assignments to each component to obtain D_i(u), the number attaining u in U_i. Store a count for each reachable total score, starting with count 1 at c_0. statement: PROOF. (1) Pick r linearly independent rows, M in Z^{r x n}. Each row satisfies W_j = a_j M with a_j in Q^r; let D be a common denominator so that D a_j is integral. For s(x) = Mx, W_j.x = a_j.s(x). (2) Hence [W_j.x >= t_j] = [(D a_j).s >= D t_j], so every gate, f and the atom sigma(x) depend on x only through s(x). (3) DP: N_0(s) = [s = 0]; N_{i+1}(s) = N_i(s) + N_i(s - M_{.,i+1}), exact integer arithmetic, N_i(s) = #{(x_1..x_i) : sum_k M_{.,k} x_k = s}. (4) After i steps every coordinate of s lies in [-Bi, Bi], so at most (2Bi+1)^r states, and at most 2^i states are reachable; total cost poly(m,n,r) times bit cost, which is O(r log(Bn)) bits for D a_j and D t_j (Cramer bound), giving poly * min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^r). (5) #SAT = sum_s N_n(s) [F(s) = 1]; N(A) = sum_{s: sigma(s)=A} N_n(s). Both read the same table. QED. CONSEQUENCE: if r <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bn+1), time = poly * 2^{(1-delta)n} = 2^n / n^{omega(1)}. This subsumes the r-distinct-forms subclass S0027 (rank <= r there), with the new bound never worse.

statement_start: Let W be an m-by-n integer matrix whose columns take at most h distinct values, and let F
statement: Let W be an m-by-n integer matrix whose columns take at most h distinct values, and let F:{0,1}^m→{0,1} be any exactly evaluable predicate. Then # {x∈{0,1}^n : F(Wx)=1} can be computed exactly with at most ∏_{a=1}^h(q_a+1) ≤ (n+1)^h table states, where q_a is the multiplicity of distinct column c_a. Proof: Partition coordinates into classes I_a of identical columns c_a, with |I_a|=q_a. For each class, selecting k_a coordinates contributes binomial(q_a,k_a) assignments and adds k_a c_a to Wx. Enumerate all count vectors (k_1,...,k_h), multiplying the binomial multiplicities. Each Boolean assignment has a unique count vector, so this enumeration counts each assignment exactly once. For each vector evaluate F(Σ_a k_a c_a), and sum the multiplicity precisely when it equals 1. There are ∏_a(q_a+1)≤(n+1)^h vectors. Multiplicities and their sums are at most 2^n and use O(n) bits; the runtime is polynomial for fixed h, times the encoded cost of evaluating F. This yields exact counting for this subclass; it does not establish the general rank-r bound.

label: S0001
statement: LEMMA (rank-r DP, subclass lane D). Let U in Z^{m x r}, A in Z^{r x n} with all |A_ik| <= a, t in Z^m, v in Z^m, T in Z, and f(x) = [sum_j v_j [U_j . (A x) >= t_j] >= T] for x in {0,1}^n. Then #{x : f(x)=1} is computed EXACTLY by the DP C_0 = {0 -> 1}, C_i(y) = C_{i-1}(y) + C_{i-1}(y - A_i) (A_i = i-th column of A), followed by the sum over y of C_n(y) [top(y) >= T], where top(y) = sum_j v_j [U_j . y >= t_j]. Correctness: f depends on x only through y = Ax, so the count equals sum_y N(y) g(y) with N(y) = #{x: Ax = y} = C_n(y) by the recurrence. Cost: each support set has entries in [-i a, i a]^r, so |supp C_i| <= (2 i a + 1)^r and the total time is O(n m r (2na+1)^r) arithmetic operations on integers of O(log(n a m)) bits. Consequence: for r <= (1-eps) n / log2(2na+1) and a <= poly(n) the time is 2^{(1-eps) n} poly(n, m), a saving of 2^{eps n} = n^{omega(1)} over brute force on the subclass of THR o THR circuits whose bottom weight matrix has rank at most r. Verified only on the tested cases (405 exact checks, n <= 12, r in {1,2,3}; cm-2cd5c456ea174b3b). Scope: this is the rank class only; it does not transfer to general THR o THR of size n^alpha, so it does not by itself meet the Chen-Tal-Wang threshold.

structure.gap: Open: (i) the generalisation to near-low-rank weight matrices (W = UA + E with E sparse or small in a suitable norm, with exact correction); (ii) whether a Chen-Tal-Wang-style transfer applies to any structured subclass of rank o(n / log n) with m = n^alpha; (iii) the full-rank case, where the DP state count is not bounded below 2^n by this method (generic full-rank runs gave no saving; peak state counts for full rank were not measured).

statement: S0002 LEMMA (column-sparse correction of the rank-r DP; closes sub-item (i) of G0001). Let W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= a, v,t in Z^m, T in Z, f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. Let S subset [n], |S| = s, B = [n]\S, q = n-s, and let r = rank of W restricted to columns B (r may be 0). Let A in Z^{r x q} be r linearly independent rows of W_B (so |A_ik| <= a), and U in Q^{m x r} with W_B = U A (exists because the rows of A span the row space of W_B). Let C_0 = {0:1}, C_i(y) = C_{i-1}(y) + C_{i-1}(y - A_i), where A_i is the i-th column of A. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} = sum over xi in {0,1}^S and y in Z^r of C_q(y) * [sum_j v_j [U_j.y >= t_j - W_{jS}.xi] >= T]. PROOF: write x = (x_B, xi). Then W_j.x = U_j.(A x_B) + W_{jS}.xi, so the indicator depends on x_B only through y = A x_B. By induction on i (split on the last bit), C_i(y) = #{x' in {0,1}^i : A_{<=i} x' = y}, so summing over xi and y gives the count. COST: |y_k| <= q a, so supp C_i lies in [-ia, ia]^r, size <= (2qa+1)^r; total 2^s (2qa+1)^r * O(q m r) operations on numbers of poly(n, log a) bits (U rational, thresholds compared exactly). CONSEQUENCE: if s + r log2(2qa+1) <= (1-eps) n - O(log n), then time 2^{(1-eps) n} poly(n,m), a saving of n^{omega(1)} for constant eps. Special cases: s = 0 gives S0001; r = 0 gives 2^s. SCOPE LIMIT: for generic full-rank W (r = q, a >= 1) the condition fails, since s + q log2(2qa+1) > n; so no saving on generic instances, and this does NOT meet the Chen-Tal-Wang threshold by itself. Corrects the turn-5 wording: the 2^s factor enumerates xi in {0,1}^S, not 'distinct y-values'. Evidence: 200 exact checks against brute force, n <= 10, s <= 3, r <= 2, 0 mismatches (cm-8d5065fab59f4e01). Also the exact row-basis reduction with rational U: 150 checks, 0 mismatches (cm-08114e1941b648c9). Status: CLAIMED, not reviewed; the proving session may not review it.

label: S0019
statement: LEMMA (rank-after-deletion DP; repairs the open generalisation G0001(i)). Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] with W an m x n integer matrix, all |entries| <= a, and let C be any column set with |C| = c. Put W' = W restricted to the columns outside C, n' = n - c, and k = rank_Q(W'). Then #f can be computed exactly in time 2^c * poly(m, n) * (2 a n' + 1)^k. PROOF: (1) For each of the 2^c assignments x_C, the bottom thresholds become integers t'_j = t_j - W_j|C . x_C. (2) Pick k linearly independent rows B_1..B_k of W' (integer). Each row W'_j = sum_l c_jl B_l with rational c_jl, computed exactly once. (3) Process the n' free variables in a fixed order. The state after a prefix is y = (B_l . x_prefix)_l. Its coordinates satisfy |y_l| <= a * (prefix length), so at most (2 a n' + 1)^k states occur per prefix; each step adds B_l[i] * bit to y. (4) At the end, W'_j . x = sum_l c_jl y_l, so f(x) = [sum_j v_j [c_j . y >= t'_j] >= T] depends on x only through y. A DP with multiplicities summed over states gives the exact count. (5) Summing over the 2^c branches gives the count. CONSEQUENCES: (a) If W = P + E with rank_Q(P) <= r and E supported on a set of columns C, then k <= r, giving the S0002 column-sparse bound. (b) If E is supported on rows R x columns C of a bipartite vertex cover, then for j not in R the rows of W' agree with P' (rank <= r), so k <= r + |R| and the time is 2^c (2 a n' + 1)^(r + |R|). (c) Choosing C adaptively to minimise c + k log2(2 a n' + 1) gives exponent min_C [ c + k(C) log2(2a(n-c)+1) ]. LIMITS: for generic full-rank W, k = n', and the bound is 2^c (2an'+1)^(n'), which is worse than brute force when a >= 1. The lemma closes only the bounded-vertex-cover case of G0001(i). Entrywise-small (norm-sparse) E and the full-rank case G0001(iii) remain open.

statement: CLAIMED (unreviewed, subclass only, likely folklore). Statement: let W in Z^{m x n} with |W_jk| <= a, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, F(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] for x in {0,1}^n. Let 1 <= c <= n and r = rank of the m x c prefix block W[:, 1..c]. Then #F = sum_x F(x) is computed exactly in time O(2^(n-c) (2ac+1)^r m (n+r)) plus poly(m,n) preprocessing. Proof: choose rows J_1..J_r of W[:,1..c] forming a basis of its row space (greedy elimination over Q). For every row j there is a unique lambda_j in Q^r with W_j,[1..c] = sum_i lambda_ji W_J_i,[1..c]; compute it by exact elimination and clear denominators (integer vector lamInt_j and denominator d_j). Write x = (y, z), y in {0,1}^c, z in {0,1}^(n-c). Put sigma(y)_i = sum_k W_J_i,k y_k. label: S0029
statement: CLAIMED: Cover-DP lemma (partial repair of G0001(i), restricted form). Let W = BC + E in Z^{m x n} with B in Z^{m x r}, C in Z^{r x n}, all entries of B, C, W bounded in absolute value by M, and E nonzero only on rows R (|R| = k) and column c0. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly by a DP over prefix states s_i = (C x_{<i}, (W_R x_{<i}), x_{c0}). Proof: (1) for j not in R, W_j.x = sum_q B_jq (Cx)_q + E_{j,c0} x_{c0}, so the gate value depends only on (Cx, x_{c0}); for j in R it is the coordinate of W_R x; hence the final state determines every gate value and f(x). (2) Transitions: s_{i+1} is a function of s_i and x_i, so the DP is exact (sum of counts over final states with f = 1). (3) Each coordinate of Cx and W_R x lies in [-Mn, Mn], so the number of states S satisfies S <= 2 (2Mn+1)^{r+k}. Time O(n * S * m * (r+k)). Consequence: #SAT in time 2^n / n^{omega(1)} whenever (r+k) log2(2Mn+1) <= n - omega(log n). Verification: exact agreement with brute force on 40 + 60 random instances (cm-1a3e813184fc44ea, cm-af453db203f14eb8, 0 mismatches); measured state counts stay below the bound (cm-53372d1d92c24fb8: n in {6..12}, r in {1,2}, k in {0,1}, e.g. n=12, r=1, k=1: max 240 states vs bound 18818 and 2^12 = 4096). GAP: this is a restatement of the rank-plus-cover saving (G0014) with an explicit state count. It does not handle generic full-rank W, where r+k is about n and S is at least 2^n. It does not close G0001(i) for general sparse E (only E on k rows plus one column), and it does not close G0001(iii) or G0013. NOT CLOSED: no closure claimed; the step is CLAIMED until a different session reviews it.

label: S0031
statement: RANK-r DP THEOREM (ALGORITHM). Setting: W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B, rank(W) = r; integers t_j, v_j, T; f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n; #SAT = #f^{-1}(1). ALGORITHM: (1) choose r rows C_1..C_r of W forming a basis of the row space (exact Gaussian elimination over Q); choose pivot columns P with C[:,P] invertible. (2) For each j put lambda_j^T = W_j[P] (C[:,P])^{-1}; then W_j = lambda_j^T C exactly (verified). Clear denominators: A_j = D*lambda_j in Z^r, TH_j = D*t_j, D a positive integer. (3) DP: table of pairs (y, cnt), start {(0,1)}; for i = 1..n replace the table by {(y,c) and (y + C[:,i], c)} with equal y merged by summing counts. (4) Output sum of cnt over table entries y with [sum_j v_j [A_j.y >= TH_j] >= T]. CORRECTNESS: y(x) = Cx, so W_j.x = lambda_j.y(x), and A_j.y >= TH_j iff W_j.x >= t_j (D > 0). By induction the table after variables 1..l holds the fibre counts of y_l = sum_{i<=l} C[:,i] x_i, so step (4) equals sum_x f(x). COMPLEXITY: |table_l| <= min(2^l, (2Bl+1)^r) since |y_{l,k}| <= B l. Time = poly(n, m, r, log B, bitsize(t,v)) * min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^r), where the bit sizes of A_j, TH_j are poly(r, log B) by Cramer's rule. COROLLARY 1: if B <= n^{O(1)} and r <= (1-eps) n / log2(2Bn+1), the time is 2^n * 2^{-eps n} * poly(n,m) = 2^n / n^{omega(1)}. COROLLARY 2: if r = o(n / log n) and B = poly(n), the time is 2^{o(n)} poly(m). m = n^alpha is arbitrary. SCOPE: exact for every W; for full-rank W the state bound is 2^n, so there is no saving. This is a counting algorithm on a restricted class, not a circuit lower bound and not a P vs NP statement. Barrier label: no barrier is relevant to a counting algorithm on a restricted class. Literature: the low-rank DP is probably folklore and has not been source-checked; the new content is the explicit bound for G0002. NEXT (enriched version, not claimed): XOR_2 o THR o THR with bottom ranks r1, r2 has the same DP over (y1, y2) in Z^{r1+r2}, time min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^{r1+r2}).

label: S0041
statement: PROOF. (1) Choose r linearly independent rows of W; call them C (r x n, integer, |C| <= M). Every row W_j lies in rowspace(C), so W_j = B_j C for a unique B_j in Q^r; compute B (Gaussian elimination over Q; poly bit size) and a common denominator D, so DB_j is integral. For z = Cx: W_j.x = B_j.z, so f(x) = g(Cx) with g(z) = [sum_j v_j [B_j.z >= t_j] >= T]. Hence N = sum_z cnt_n(z) g(z), where cnt_i(z) = #{x' in {0,1}^i : C_{<i} x' = z}. (2) cnt_0 = delta_0 and cnt_{i+1}(z) = cnt_i(z) + cnt_i(z - C_{.,i}); this is an exact DP over the support S_i = supp cnt_i. (3) Support bound: every z in S_i has entries in [-Mi, Mi], so |S_i| <= (2Mi+1)^r; and sum_z cnt_i(z) = 2^i with cnt_i >= 1 on S_i, so |S_i| <= 2^i. Hence |S_i| <= min(2^i, (2Mi+1)^r). (4) Each DP step touches each z in S_i with O(r) integer operations; the final sum evaluates g at S_n with O(mr) operations per point. Total: O((n+m) r * max_i |S_i|) = poly(n,m) * min(2^n, (2Mn+1)^r) operations, plus poly preprocessing. Bit sizes: cnt <= 2^n; D B_j z and D t_j are integers of size poly(n, m, log M, log D). So the arithmetic is exact in poly bit cost. (5) Corollary: r log2(2Mn+1) <= (1-delta) n gives 2^{(1-delta) n} poly; r = omega(1), r = o(n/log n), M = O(1) gives (2Mn+1)^r = 2^n / n^{omega(1)} because r log n = omega(log n) and r log n = o(n). Scope: a saving exists only for rank-r weights with r log(2Mn+1) <= (1-delta) n; full rank r = n gives the bound 2^n (no saving). Relation: the state bound is the one recorded in S0004 (D_x <= (kW+1)^r); the new content is the DP recurrence with its running time, which is the procedure G0002 asks for.

label: S0055
statement: ALGORITHM (block-DP counting for THR o THR, CLAIMED, pending review). Input: W in Z^{m x n} with |W_ij| <= M, thresholds t, weights v in Z^m, T. Let N subset [n] be a column block with rank_Q(W_N) = r' and C = [n] \ N, c = |C|. Choose r' independent rows R = W_{I,N} of W_N (integer), and a rational Lambda with W_N = Lambda R (exists because every row of W_N lies in the row space of R); scale Lambda by a common denominator D so Lambda' = D Lambda is integral. For x = (x_C, x_N): (Wx)_j = a_j(x_C) + (Lambda y)_j with a = W_C x_C and y = R x_N in Z^{r'}, |y_i| <= M|N|. ALGORITHM: for each x_C in {0,1}^c, run a DP over the columns of N that computes D(y) = #{x_N : R x_N = y} with states in Z^{r'} (at most (2M|N|+1)^{r'} of them); output sum over x_C and y of D(y) * [sum_j v_j [a_j + (Lambda y)_j / D >= t_j] >= T]. CORRECTNESS: the summand depends on x only through (x_C, y), and D groups the x_N by y, so the sum equals #{x : sum_j v_j [(Wx)_j >= t_j] >= T}. RUNNING TIME: O(2^c * |N| * S * m * r') with S <= (2M|N|+1)^{r'}; for constant r' and M = poly(n) this is 2^{n-|N|} * poly(n). Consequence: a #SAT / count procedure with a proved running time 2^{n-|N|} poly(n) whenever the bottom weight matrix has a column block of size |N| and constant rank. Evidence: cm-ffc11693d5d74022 (exact DP vs brute force, n = 10, 12, 23 instances, all_ok true; exploratory computation, not a validator claim). SCOPE AND GAP: the saving needs a constant-rank column block of linear size; random, majority, sparse and large-weight families have no such block (any |N| columns are generically independent, so S is exponential and the bound is useless). Open: whether the family of hard instances contains such blocks; whether this beats the spec's rank-one bound 2^{n-k/2} (unchecked: the comparison needs the spec text); a polynomial-time count for a block of rank r = Theta(log n). Not claimed to close an obligation; closes left empty for the reviewer to decide.

label: S0058
statement: ALGORITHM (rank-one block, CLAIMED, pending review). Let W in Z^{m x n} have entries bounded by M, and let J be a set of k columns with W_ij = a_i v_j for all i and j in J (rank one on J). For x = (x_J, x_rest), every bottom gate sees x_J only through z = sum_{j in J} v_j x_j in [-kM', kM'] where M' = max|v_j|, so (Wx)_i = (W_rest x_rest)_i + a_i z. Procedure: for each x_rest in {0,1}^{n-k}, compute the thresholded vector using a DP over J that counts #{x_J : z = s} for each integer s (O(k^2 M') states, O(k) steps, m gate checks per state). Output = sum over x_rest and s of count(s) * [sum_i u_i [(W_rest x_rest)_i + a_i s >= t_i] >= T]. Correctness: the summand depends on x only through (x_rest, z). Time 2^{n-k} * poly(n, m, k, M'). This is 2^{n-k} poly, strictly better than the spec's 2^{n-k/2} meet-in-the-middle bound when the weights are polynomially bounded. Correction of my earlier S0055: that block-DP restates the rank-r DP of R0805 / S0002 (branch on the complement, DP on the rank block) and is not new. Only this rank-one improvement is new content.

Procedure: for each x_rest in {0,1}^{n-k}, compute the thresholded vector using a DP over J that counts #{x_J : z = s} for each integer s (O(k^2 M') states, O(k) steps, m gate checks per state). Output = sum over x_rest and s of count(s) * [sum_i u_i [(W_rest x_rest)_i + a_i s >= t_i] >= T]. Correctness: the summand depends on x only through (x_rest, z). Time 2^{n-k} * poly(n, m, k, M'). This is 2^{n-k} poly, strictly better than the spec's 2^{n-k/2} meet-in-the-middle bound when the weights are polynomially bounded. Correction of my earlier S0055: that block-DP restates the rank-r DP of R0805 / S0002 (branch on the complement, DP on the rank block) and is not new. Only this rank-one improvement is new content.

label: S0060
statement: ALGORITHM (rank-one block DP, CLAIMED, pending review). Let W be an integer m x n matrix with entries bounded by M, and let J be a set of k columns with W_ij = a_i v_j for all i and j in J. For x = (x_J, x_R) we have (Wx)_i = (W_R x_R)_i + a_i z, where z = sum over j in J of v_j x_j. Procedure: compute count_J(s) = #{x_J : z = s} once by a DP over J with states in [-kM', kM'] (M' = max |v_j|). Then enumerate x_R in {0,1}^(n-k) and output the sum over integers s of count_J(s) times [sum_i u_i [(W_R x_R)_i + a_i s >= t_i] >= T]. Correctness: the summand depends on x only through (x_R, z). Time: 2^(n-k) times O(m k^2 M') arithmetic operations. This saves a factor 2^k over brute force, which is better than the spec's 2^(n-k/2) meet-in-the-middle bound. Scope: it helps only when a constant fraction of the columns is proportional, and it does not apply to full-rank families (k = 0). Classification correction: this is the block-DP of S0055 specialised to a rank-one block (branch on the complement, DP on the block). structure.lemma: RANK-r BOX-BOUND DP. Let W in Z^{m x n} have rank r and all |W_ji| <= B. Choose a row index set R with |R| = r whose rows form a basis of the row space, and let A = W_R (integer, |A_ki| <= B). For each j there is C_j in Q^r with W_j = C_j^T A (exact, since W_j lies in the row space). Then for all x in {0,1}^n: W_j . x = C_j . (A x). Hence #SAT f = sum_y c(y) g(y), where y = A x, c(y) = #{x : Ax = y}, g(y) = [sum_j v_j [C_j . y >= t_j] >= T]. The DP over columns i = 1..n keeps a dictionary {y: c(y)} and adds column A_i (for x_i = 0 and 1). The number of keys after step i is at most prod_k (sum_{i' <= i} |A_{k i'}| + 1) <= prod_k (||A_k||_1 + 1) <= (nB + 1)^r, because coordinate k of every partial sum lies in the integer interval [sum_i min(0, A_ki), sum_i max(0, A_ki)] of length ||A_k||_1. Also keys <= 2^n. So the total running time is poly(n, m) * min{2^n, (nB+1)^r} with exact rational arithmetic. Consequence: for r <= (1 - delta) n / log2(nB + 1), the time is 2^{(1-delta) n} * poly(n, m), i.e. a saving of 2^{delta n} / poly over brute force. This refines the earlier (2na+1)^r bound, since ||A_k||_1 <= n a.

label: S0065
statement: COLUMN-DELETION RANK LEMMA. Let W in Z^{m x n} with |W_ji| <= B. Let S subset [n], |S| = s, R = [n] minus S, and suppose rank(W_R) <= r, where W_R is W with the columns in S deleted. Let A be a set of rank(W_R) rows of W_R forming a basis of its row space. Entries of A are rows of W, so |A_ki| <= B. For each row j there is C_j in Q^r with W_jR = C_j^T A (exact, since W_jR lies in the row space). For x in {0,1}^n write x = (x_R, x_S). Then W_j . x = C_j . (A x_R) + W_jS . x_S. Let c(y) = #{x_R : A x_R = y} and g(z) = [sum_j v_j [z_j >= t_j] >= T], with z_j = C_j . y + W_jS . x_S compared exactly over Q. Then #{x : g(Wx)} = sum over x_S in {0,1}^s of sum over y of c(y) g(C y + W_S x_S). The DP over the columns of R keeps the dictionary {y: c(y)} and adds column A_i for x_i in {0,1}. Coordinate k of every partial sum lies in an integer interval of length ||A_k||_1 <= |R| B, so the number of keys is at most prod_k (||A_k||_1 + 1) <= (|R| B + 1)^r, and also at most 2^{|R|}. Hence the total time is O(2^s (|R| B + 1)^r poly(m, n)) with exact rational arithmetic. Special cases: s = 0 is the rank-r DP lemma (Q-9d5ab93ad8 lemma). If W = C A + E with E having k nonzero entries in total, then deleting the at most k columns touched by E leaves a matrix of rank <= r, so s <= k and the time is 2^k (nB+1)^r poly. This beats 2^n when k + r log2(nB+1) <= (1 - delta) n.

label: S0068
statement: LEMMA (column-deletion rank-r reduction). For W in Z^{m x n} with |W_ji| <= B and r >= 0, define rho_r(W) = min{|S| : rank(W restricted to columns [n] minus S) <= r}. Then for any thresholds t, weights v >= 0 and T, the count #SAT = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T} equals sum over x_S in {0,1}^S of #{x' in {0,1}^{[n]\S} : sum_j v_j [W'_j . x' >= t_j - W_{j,S} . x_S] >= T}, where W' = W restricted to [n]\S. Each inner count is a count for the rank-<=r matrix W' with integer thresholds, so the rank-r box-bound DP applies to it, giving total time 2^{rho} * poly(n,m) * (nB+1)^r for a set S attaining rho. PROOF: partition x = (x_S, x'); the gate condition W_j . x >= t_j is equivalent to W'_j . x' >= t_j - W_{j,S} . x_S, and the outer sum over x_S is exhaustive. The identity holds for every S, not only the minimal one; minimality only minimises the 2^{|S|} factor. Corollary (E = W - W0 with rank(W0) <= r and at most e nonzero entries): S = columns touched by E gives rho_r(W) <= e, so the cost is 2^e * poly * (nB+1)^r, and S can be found by enumerating column sets of size <= e (n^e choices), giving a promise-free algorithm of time n^{O(e)} * 2^e * poly * (nB+1)^r. This subsumes S0002 (column-supported E) and covers entrywise-sparse E.

Generic full-rank W has rho_r(W) = n - r (deleting s columns leaves rank min(m, n-s) > r unless s >= n-r), so the lemma gives no saving on generic full-rank instances: G0001(iii) stays open, now equivalent to showing hard instances have rho_r(W) >= (1 - delta) n for every r = o(n / log n) with fixed bit-size B. The reduction is not a speed-up for the full-rank case.

label: S0076
statement: CLAIMED: Subclass algorithm. Setting: W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji| <= B_W, thresholds t_j, unit top weights, threshold T. K = exceptional rows (|K| = k); every j outside K has W_j = U_j A with A in Z^{r x n}, |A_ic| <= B_A, U_j in Z^r. Repaired DP key after x_1..x_p: (cnt = number of decided-true rows in K, y = A x_{<=p} in Z^r, sorted tuple of (q, s_q) for undecided q in K with exact partial sums). Claim 1': #keys at step p <= (k+1)(2pB_A+1)^r prod_{q in K}((n-p)B_W+1). Proof: cnt in {0..k}; y in [-pB_A, pB_A]^r; an undecided q has s_q in the window [t_q - L+_q(p), t_q - L-_q(p) - 1], of length at most (n-p)B_W. Claim 2': count = sum of weights of final keys with cnt + #{j outside K: U_j.y >= t_j} >= T; exact because the future outcome of every row is a function of the key and the remaining bits, and all rows are decided at p = n. Time O(n m k (k+1)(2nB_A+1)^r (nB_W+1)^k) with exact integers, so 2^{(1-eps)n} whenever (r+k) log2(2nB+1) <= (1-eps)n - O(log n). Scope: covers only THR o THR with low rank plus few exceptional rows; full rank is not covered. It does not close G0001(iii), G0003 or G0006.

label: S0084
statement: LEMMA-BLOCK (lane D, CLAIMED). Setup: W in Z^{m x n} with |W_{j,i}| <= B; t in Z^m; v in Z_{>=0}^m; T in Z; f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. Let R subset [n], |R| = q, S = [n] minus R, and r = rank_Q(W_R), where W_R is the m x q submatrix on columns R. Claim: #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computable exactly in time 2^{n-q} * (2Bq+1)^r * poly(m, n, log B) arithmetic operations (exact rationals). Proof: (1) choose rows P = {P_1..P_r} with W_{P,R} a basis of the row space of W_R; each row satisfies W_{j,R} = sum_p lambda_{jp} W_{P_p,R} with unique lambda_j in Q^r, computable by Gaussian elimination in poly time. (2) For x_R in {0,1}^q set y_p = W_{P_p,R}.x_R, an integer with |y_p| <= Bq, so y lies in a set Y of size at most (2Bq+1)^r. (3) For x = (x_R, z), z = x_S: W_j.x = c_j(z) + sum_p lambda_{jp} y_p, with c_j(z) = W_{j,S}.z. Hence f(x) depends only on (z, y). (4) N(y) = #{x_R : y(x_R) = y} is computed by a DP over the q columns of R: each column adds W_{P,c} to the current states, so the state set stays inside Y, with cost O(q (2Bq+1)^r r). (5) Count = sum over z in {0,1}^{|S|} and y in Y with N(y) > 0 of N(y) * [sum_j v_j [c_j(z) + lambda_j.y >= t_j] >= T]; each term costs O(m r). Total time 2^{n-q} * (2Bq+1)^r * poly. QED. Corollary (subclass C(delta, eps)): for R of size q = delta n and rank r <= eps n / log2(2B delta n + 1), the count takes time 2^{(1-delta+eps) n} * poly(n) for constant B or B = poly(n). The case S empty (R = [n]) recovers the rank-r DP of cm-2cd5c456ea174b3b. The new content is the split: column-branching on S combined with the rank-DP on R, so the 2^{n-q} term and the (2Bq+1)^r term are both controlled.

label: S0093
statement: CLAIM (new, unreviewed; builds on S0081 SURVIVED_REVIEW): Procedure FWD counts #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} exactly by a forward DP over the prefix-state vectors sigma_p = (W_{j,<=p}.x_{<=p})_j in Z^m: start with {0: 1}; at step p, each state sigma with multiplicity c yields sigma and sigma + W_{:,p}, each with multiplicity c; at the end, sum the multiplicities of the states with sum_j v_j [sigma_j >= t_j] >= T. Correctness is by induction on p. Time: O(n m N*) where N* = max_p N_p and N_p = number of distinct prefix states at prefix p. Theorem: if W = UA + E with A an r x n integer matrix of entries in [-B,B], E supported on columns in a set T with s + r log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-eps) n, then N* <= 2^{(1-eps) n} (by S0081 at each p), so the running time is O(n m 2^{(1-eps) n}) with no knowledge of the decomposition. label: S0098
statement: LEMMA (rank-r Cramer DP, exact, no factor hypothesis). Let n, m, r >= 1, W in Z^{m x n} with rank W = r and B = max |W_ji|, B >= 1. Let t, v in Z^m and T in Z. Then N(W,t,v,T) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T} is computable exactly in time poly(m, n, log B) * (2an+1)^r, where a = r^{(r+1)/2} B^r. PROOF. (1) Choose rows R and columns C with Q = W[R,C] nonsingular (|R| = |C| = r; exists since rank r). Put d = det Q != 0 and N := adj(Q) W[R,:] in Z^{r x n}. (2) For every row j: W[j,C] = alpha_j^T Q for alpha_j = Q^{-T} W[j,C]^T, and W[R,:] has rank r, so W_j = W[j,C] Q^{-1} W[R,:]. Multiplying by d: d W_j = c_j N with c_j := W[j,C] in Z^{1 x r}. (3) Hence for y := N x in Z^r: W_j . x >= t_j iff c_j . y >= d t_j when d > 0 (reversed when d < 0). The right side is an integer, so this test is exact. Define g_j(y) := [sign(d)(c_j . y - d t_j) >= 0]. (4) The count equals sum over y of c_n(y) * [sum_j v_j g_j(y) >= T], where c_p(y) = #{x_{<=p} : N_{<=p} x_{<=p} = y}. Each c_p is computed by the recurrence c_{p+1}(y) = c_p(y) + c_p(y - N_{:,p+1}), with states y in Z^r. (5) Bounds: |N_ki| <= r * max|minor_{r-1}(Q)| * B <= r * (r-1)^{(r-1)/2} B^{r-1} * B <= a. Hence |y_k| <= a p at prefix p, and the number of states is at most (2ap+1)^r (and at most 2^p). Total work: O(n S r + S m r) integer operations with S = (2an+1)^r, plus polynomial Gaussian elimination over Q to find R, C, Q. Correctness is exact, since every step is an identity over Z. CONSEQUENCES: (a) for constant r and B = poly(n) the time is poly(n); (b) the time is 2^{(1-eps) n} poly whenever r * log2(2an+1) <= (1-eps) n, i.e. r (log2(2n+1) + ((r+1)/2) log2 r + r log2 B + 1) <= (1-eps) n. For B = O(1) this holds for r <= c sqrt(n / log n). The lemma replaces the hypothesis 'W = UA with small A' of the CLAIMED rank-r DP, and it does not need the factor bound to be an input.

statement: LEMMA R (rank-r DP with state bound (2Bn+1)^r; replaces the bound of S0098, whose a = r^((r+1)/2) B^r is not needed). Let W in Z^{m x n} with rank W = r >= 1, B = max |W_ji| >= 1, t, v in Z^m, T in Z. (2) Each row satisfies W_j = W[j,C] Q^{-1} W_R, since restricting to columns C gives W[j,C] = W[j,C] Q^{-1} Q. Multiplying by d: d W_j = g_j W_R with g_j := W[j,C] adj(Q) in Z^{1 x r}. label: S0106
statement: THEOREM (rank-r DP). Let W in Z^{m x n} with |W_jl| <= B, rank_Q(W) = r, and let t_j, v_j, T be rationals/integers. Then N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly in O(n * m * r * (2Bn+1)^r) rational operations on numbers of bit-size poly(n, log B). PROOF. (1) Greedily choose row indices I = {k_1..k_r} with W_{k_1..k_r} linearly independent; they span the row space of W. (2) For each j there is a unique c_j in Q^r with W_j = sum_l c_jl W_{k_l} (existence: spanning; uniqueness: independence). (3) Put s(x) = W_I x in Z^r. Then W_j.x = c_j.s(x), so [W_j.x >= t_j] = [c_j.s(x) >= t_j] depends only on s(x). Hence N = sum_s D(s) g(s), where D(s) = #{x : W_I x = s} and g(s) = [sum_j v_j [c_j.s >= t_j] >= T]. (4) DP over columns i = 1..n: D_0 = delta_0, D_i(s) = D_{i-1}(s) + D_{i-1}(s - col_i), where col_i = (W_{k_l,i})_l. This is exact. (5) For x in {0,1}^n, |W_{k_l}.x| <= Bn, so every reachable state lies in [-Bn, Bn]^r: at most (2Bn+1)^r states at each step. (6) For r <= (1-eps) n / log2(2Bn+1), (2Bn+1)^r <= 2^{(1-eps)n}. With B = poly(n) this range is r = (1-eps) n / O(log n), for any m (m enters only polynomially). The coefficient denominators have bit-size O(r log(Bn)) = poly(n), so the arithmetic overhead is polynomial. SCOPE: exact rank r only. Full rank (G0001 iii) and near-low-rank (G0001 i) are NOT covered. The bound uses only r, not the structure of the thresholds. SUPERSEDES: the sqrt(n/log n) range in the earlier gap, which came from a Hadamard bound on coefficients that the argument does not need. EVIDENCE: exact correctness only, cm-f7bdefcc1a624fd1 (120 random rank<=3 instances, n in 3..8, DP vs brute force, 0 failures). Timing is exploration only and is not cited as support for speed. Correctness is also proved by (1)-(4). thr2_evaluate measurement is pending; its families are generic full-rank, so it cannot test this subclass as provided.

label: S0108
statement: EXTENSION (rank-r DP with s free columns). Let W in Z^{m x n} with |W_jl| <= B. Let the first s columns be arbitrary and let the submatrix W' = W[:, s+1..n] have rank_Q r. Then N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly with at most 2^s (2Bn+1)^r reachable states per column step, i.e. O(n m r 2^s (2Bn+1)^r) rational operations. PROOF. Enumerate the prefix xs in {0,1}^s (2^s choices). For fixed xs, the prefix contribution g_j(xs) = sum_{i<=s} W_ji xs_i is a fixed integer. Apply steps (1)-(5) of S0106 to W' (rows I of W' span its row space; W'_j = sum_l c_jl W'_{k_l}; state sv = W'_I x_suffix in Z^r with |sv_l| <= B(n-s)). Then W_j.x = c_j.sv + g_j(xs), so the indicator depends only on (xs, sv). Summing the DP counts over states with the condition gives N exactly. The state count is at most 2^s (2Bn+1)^r. SCOPE: column-support perturbation only (the non-rank part is confined to s columns); it does not give the entrywise near-low-rank form W = UA + E of G0001(i), and it does not cover full rank. Saving holds when s + r log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-eps) n, e.g. s = eps' n gives r <= (1 - eps - eps') n / log2(2Bn+1). EVIDENCE: exact correctness only, cm-aac7b94520a54ee7 (80 random instances, n in 4..8, s in 0..3, r in 1..3; 0 failures; max state ratio 0.545). Timing is not cited as support. Not reviewed; CLAIMED and open until another session reviews it.
