label: S0119
statement: L2 (meet-in-the-middle with partition-tree range counting, constant rank r). Let W = UA with U in Z^{m x r}, A in Z^{r x n}, t in Z^m, v in Z^m, T in Z; f(x) = [sum_j v_j [U_j.(Ax) >= t_j] >= T]. Fix r >= 1 constant. Split x = (x1, x2) with x1 in {0,1}^h, x2 in {0,1}^u, h + u = n, and let Y2 = {A_2 x2 : x2 in {0,1}^u} (a weighted point set of at most 2^u points in R^r). Then #f = sum over x1 of W(Y2 + A_1 x1), where W(z) = number of points of Y2 with [U_j.(z+y) >= t_j] pattern giving F=1. Claim: the cells of the arrangement {U_j.z = t_j - U_j.(A_1x1)} partition R^r into O(m^r) cells, each triangulated into O(m^r) simplices in total (constant r), and the weighted count of Y2 in each simplex is one simplex-range-counting query (Matousek 1992 partition tree: O(N) preprocessing, O(N^{1-1/r} polylog) per query, constant r). statement: ALGORITHM (rank-r residual DP for THR o THR #SAT). Setting: f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n, W in Z^{m x n} with |W_jk| <= b, rank_Q(W) = r, integers t_j, v_j, T. PROOF. (1) Gaussian elimination picks r independent rows of W, indices basis, A = those rows (integer, |A_kl| <= b), and pivot columns P (the reduced rows restricted to P are triangular with nonzero diagonal, so M = A[:,P] is invertible). (2) Every row of W lies in the row space of A, so W_j = U_j A with U_j = W_j[P] M^{-1} in Q^r. Put den_j = lcm of denominators of U_j and c_j = den_j U_j in Z^r. With z(x) = A x in Z^r: W_j.x >= t_j iff c_j.z >= den_j t_j. So f(x) is a function of z(x) only. (3) |z_k(x)| <= n b, so z ranges over a set of size S <= (2nb+1)^r. (4) DP over i = 1..n keeps, exactly, a map from partial sums z_{<i} to the number of prefixes realising them (states at most S); the update adds A_i (column i of A). At the end, sum the multiplicities of states z with f(z) = 1. This is exact. Running time: n * S * poly(r, m) arithmetic operations on integers of bit length poly(r, log(nb)), i.e. (2nb+1)^r * poly(m, n, r, log b) bit operations. CONSEQUENCES: rank r = o(n / log n) with b = n^{O(1)} gives 2^{o(n)} poly(m) time. Rank r <= kappa n / log n with constant b gives roughly 2^{kappa(1+o(1)) n}, which is 2^{(1-delta) n} for kappa small. (Probably folklore; not novelty-checked.)

statement: LEMMA (lane D, variable-class count, CLAIMED by the session that stated it, not yet reviewed). Let C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n, with integer weights. Suppose the variables partition into D classes C_1..C_D with sizes n_d >= 1, sum n_d = n, and every i in C_d has the same weight column c_d in Z^m (W_{j,i} = c_{d,j}). Then #SAT(C) = sum over 0<=y_d<=n_d of prod_d binom(n_d,y_d) * [sum_j v_j [sum_d y_d c_{d,j} >= t_j] >= T]. Proof: the map x -> (y_d = |x intersect C_d|) is onto, the fibre over y has prod_d binom(n_d,y_d) elements, and W_j.x = sum_d c_{d,j} y_d depends only on y. The sum has prod_d (n_d+1) terms, each costing O(mD). Bound: for x >= 1, x - log2(x+1) >= 0.415 (x-1). This holds with equality at x=2, and the derivative of the left side, 0.585, exceeds that of the right side, 1/((x+1) ln 2), for x >= 2. Multiplying over d gives prod_d (n_d+1) <= 2^{n - 0.415 (n-D)}. Therefore #SAT(C) is computable in time poly(m,D) * 2^{0.585 n + 0.415 D}, a saving of 2^{0.415 (n-D)} over brute force. The saving is superpolynomial iff n - D = omega(log n). For D = O(1) the algorithm is polynomial. Measured counts agree with the bound at all six grid points (cm-b15e97e20ccf4808, cm-7e78b5662f2d4e56).

statement: Proof. Let s_j(i) be the partial sum of gate j over the first i variables. Let P_j(i) = sum_{l>i} max(W_jl,0) and N_j(i) = sum_{l>i} min(W_jl,0), so the final sum lies in [s_j+N_j, s_j+P_j]. Define the class kappa_j(s) = 0 if s+P_j(i) < t_j; 1 if s+N_j(i) >= t_j; and the exact value s otherwise. (1) Exactness: for class 0 or 1 the bottom bit is the same for every completion of the remaining variables; for an undecided s the class is the exact value. So the bit vector of any completion depends only on the class vector. (2) Transitions are well defined: reading x_{i+1} changes P and N by subtracting max(W,0) and min(W,0) at index i+1. If class 0, then s'+P(i+1) <= s+P(i) < t, so s' stays class 0. Class 1 is symmetric. Undecided values are updated exactly. So the class vector at stage i+1 is a function of the class vector at stage i and x_{i+1}. (3) Counting: the DP c_{i+1}(kappa') = sum over (kappa, x_{i+1}) with transition kappa -> kappa' of c_i(kappa) is exact, and at i = n the classes are bits, so #f^{-1}(1) = sum of c_n over class vectors with top(bits) = 1. (4) State bound: at stage i an undecided value of gate j lies in an interval of length P_j(i) - N_j(i) = sum_{l>i}|W_jl| <= B(n-i), so there are at most B(n-i)+2 classes per gate and at most prod_j (B(n-i)+2) class vectors. Summing over i gives O(k n (Bn+2)^k) operations. Scope: fixed k, bounded integer weights; all other bottom gates are irrelevant to f and drop out. Compared with the plain partial-sum DP (state bound (2Bi+1)^k at stage i), the gain is a constant-factor change in the window, not a change of the exponent. Barrier and transfer check: this is a poly(n) algorithm for constant k and B = poly(n), so it cannot transfer to a 2^n/n^{omega(1)} lower-bound hypothesis; no LOWER_BOUND is claimed. Known-type status: counting for a constant number of halfspaces over a bounded-weight cube is standard (Dyer / Frieze-style pseudo-polynomial DP); I have not checked the literature, so novelty is unverified.

label: S0104
statement:
statement: Let F be a positive EXACT1 3-CNF on n variables and m clauses, with three distinct variables per clause. For a fixed variable order whose every prefix cut has at most B crossing clauses, exact #SAT is computable in O((n+m)(3^B+1) poly(B)) arithmetic operations, storing at most 3^B+1 states per level. Proof: At level k, store each distinct residual function F_alpha obtained by assigning the first k variables, with weight equal to the number of such prefixes. Initially store F with weight 1. For each state, branch on the next bit, form the child residual, and merge identical residuals by adding weights. Inductively, the weight of each residual is exactly the number of prefixes yielding it: branching partitions each prefix by its next bit, and merging sums disjoint sets. At level n, residuals are constants, so summing weights of residual 1 returns #SAT(F). To bound states, clauses wholly in the unprocessed variables form a common conjunct; processed-only clauses contribute only a single failure flag. Each crossing EXACT1 clause has at most three residual conditions: if one variable is processed, the remaining pair must sum to 0 or 1; if two are processed, the remaining variable is fixed to 0 or 1, or the condition is false. Thus there are at most 3^B tuples when the flag is true and one zero residual when it is false. Canonical child descriptions can be formed by scanning clauses and recording these forms, giving the stated bound with polynomial-in-B overhead. This proves the algorithm only for the stated bounded-crossing, fixed-order subclass and makes no claim relating B to rational cut rank.
proof: Full induction and state bound are included in the statement.

label: S0115
statement:
statement: Let F be a conjunction of m positive EXACT1 clauses, each on three distinct Boolean variables, and fix a variable order whose every prefix cut has at most B crossing clauses. Then #SAT(F) is computable by a dynamic program using at most 2^B states per level and O((m+n(B+1))2^B) arithmetic operations, excluding integer bit complexity and representation overhead.
proof: At each prefix cut, store the partial sum of assigned variables for each crossing clause. Reject any prefix with a partial sum at least 2. For each remaining state, branch on the next variable's two values, update only clauses incident to that variable, and when a clause's last variable is assigned retain the branch exactly when its total sum is 1. Clauses wholly in the unprocessed suffix are untouched. Hence the vector of active sums, each in {0,1}, determines all constraints involving processed variables that can affect a completion. Prefixes with the same vector have the same valid suffix completions, so their counts may be added. There are at most 2^B vectors per level. Each clause-variable incidence is updated once per state at its variable's level; summing degrees gives O(m 2^B) incidence work. Explicit state-vector updates cost O(B) per state per level, hence O(n B 2^B); initialization and finalization add O((m+n)2^B). The total is O((m+n(B+1))2^B). At the final level all clauses have been checked, so the accumulated count is exactly #SAT(F).

statement: INTERVAL-FRONTIER-DP (CLAIMED). Scope: C(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j . x_{I_j} >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n, I_j = [a_j, a_j+k_j), k_j <= K, |W_{j,i}| <= B, V = sum_j |v_j|, D = max over cuts l of the number of j with a_j < l < a_j+k_j. Claim: #C is computed exactly by a left-to-right frontier DP with at most (2V+1)(BK+2)^D states per cut, total time poly(n,m)(2V+1)(BK+2)^D. Proof: the state at cut l is P (sum of v_j g_j over finished gates, in [-V,V]) and, for each active gate, s_j = clamp(t_j - W_prefix . rho, [L_j, U_j+1]), where L_j, U_j are min and max of W_rem . y. Clamping is exact: s_j <= L_j means constant 1 on the remaining cube, s_j > U_j means constant 0. The residual is determined by (P, s_j). Reading x_l updates s_j by subtracting W_{j,l} x_l, finishes or starts gates locally, and re-clamps, so the next state depends only on the current state and x_l. Counts propagate with multiplicities. Each clamped s_j has at most U_j - L_j + 2 <= BK+2 values. Consequence: 2^{o(n)} poly time when D log(BK+2) = o(n); for uniformly spread intervals with m = n^1.5 and bounded K, D = O(sqrt(n) K), which qualifies. Gap: does NOT cover arbitrary supports, XOR_2, or the generic class; does NOT close G0001 or G0002, since the overlap D is not controlled for general supports.

label: S0101
statement: THEOREM (bounded-support frontier DP). Let C(x)=[sum_{j=1}^m v_j 1{sum_{i in S_j} w_{ji}x_i >= t_j} >= T] on {0,1}^n, where each S_j is arbitrary with |S_j|<=K, integer coefficients, B=max(1,max|w_{ji}|), and V=sum_j |v_j|. Fix an order; A_l is the gates with support on both sides of cut l, and D=max_l|A_l|. Then #C is exactly computable in time poly(n,m,K,bitlength)(2V+1)(BK+2)^D. At cut l store P, the weighted sum of gates whose last support variable is processed, and for each crossing gate j store z_j=clamp(t_j-a_j,[L_j,U_j+1]), where a_j is its processed score and [L_j,U_j] the exact range of its remaining score. Thresholds <=L_j represent constant 1; thresholds >U_j represent constant 0; interior thresholds are retained exactly. Thus the state determines the residual outer predicate. Upon reading the next bit, update incident scores and recompute/clamp remaining ranges. A gate whose last support variable is read is evaluated and added to P; one whose first support variable is read enters the frontier. Empty-support gates are evaluated initially. Induction on cuts proves equal states have identical residual predicates; propagating prefix multiplicities counts every assignment once. Since U_j-L_j<=BK, each active coordinate has at most BK+2 values, while P has at most 2V+1 values. Transitions are computable in polynomial time. It is subexponential if D log(BK+2)+log(2V+1)=o(n), up to polynomial factors. No useful K,D bounds are asserted for general THR o THR.

structure.evidence: The complete state invariant and transition induction are in the statement. This removes the interval-support restriction and handles arbitrary supports under explicit bounded-size and bounded-crossing hypotheses, narrowing G0046 to finding such hypotheses for the target class.

label: S0010
statement:
statement: Let t>=d>=1, M=sum_{j=0}^d binom(t,j), and r=ceil(2^(2d)(2 ln M+2)). A hitting set for every nonzero multilinear polynomial over any field with at most two monomials of degree <=d can be deterministically constructed using O(r*2^t*M^2) arithmetic operations and r output points. Proof: define requirements R consisting of each support S (|S|<=d), requiring at least one sampled point A to contain S, and each unordered distinct pair S,T, requiring a sampled point A to contain exactly one of S,T. For a partial sequence h of k points, let Phi(h) be the sum, over unmet requirements R, of the conditional probability that R remains unmet after r-k independent uniformly random points. For each candidate next point A in {0,1}^t, compute Phi(hA). Their average over uniform A is Phi(h), so some candidate has Phi(hA)<=Phi(h); choose one. Initially Phi(empty) <= (M+M^2)*exp(-r*2^(-d-1)) < 1. After r choices Phi<1; any unmet requirement would contribute 1, so all are met. A hit detects a one-term polynomial; separation detects a two-term polynomial over every field. There are O(M^2) requirements, r rounds, 2^t candidates per round, and each score costs O(M^2), giving the stated bound. This is not a polynomial-time PIT bound in general t and closes no P-vs-NP obligation.
evidence: Complete conditional-expectation argument stated above; finite corroboration for t=10,d=1 is cm-18b7a425100b4944.

label: S0012
statement:
statement: For t>=d>=1, let M=sum_{j=0}^d binom(t,j), r=ceil(2^(2d)(2 ln M+2)), and let R contain one hit requirement per support |S|<=d and one separation requirement per unordered distinct support pair. The conditional-expectation construction in S0010 can be implemented with at most O(r*2^t*M^2) integer arithmetic operations on integers of O(tr+log M) bits, hence bit complexity O(r*2^t*M^2*(tr+log M)^2) using schoolbook arithmetic, and outputs r Boolean points meeting all requirements. Proof: For each requirement j, let c_j be its exact number of satisfying points in {0,1}^t; c_j is an integer in [0,2^t]. After k selected points, if j is still unmet its conditional failure probability is ((2^t-c_j)/2^t)^(r-k), with numerator and denominator at most 2^(t(r-k)) and 2^(t(r-k)). Their sum Phi has common denominator 2^(t(r-k)), and numerator bit length O(tr+log M), since |R|<=M+M^2. For a candidate next point A, update each unmet requirement using whether A satisfies it, yielding the next potential with the common denominator 2^(t(r-k-1)); its numerator has the same bit bound. The average of these 2^t candidate potentials equals Phi, so choosing a minimizer never increases Phi. Initially Phi<1 by the union bound in S0008; after r choices Phi<1, forcing zero unmet requirements because any unmet requirement contributes 1. Enumerating all candidates and requirements at each of r rounds gives O(r*2^t*M^2) integer operations. The bit bound follows from integer numerator sizes; schoolbook multiplication/addition gives the stated conservative bit complexity. This remains exponential in t and is not a general PIT speed-up.
evidence: Derivation in the statement; S0008 supplies the probability estimates, and cm-18b7a425100b4944 independently checks only t=10,d=1.

label: S0003
statement:
PROOF. Let s(x) = (F^{(1)} x, ..., F^{(d)} x) in Z^d, and let a_i = (F_{1i}, ..., F_{di}) be the i-th column of F. Then s(x) = sum_i x_i a_i. Since g_j(x) = [s_{k(j)}(x) >= t_j], we have f(x) = h(s(x)) with h(sigma) = [sum_j v_j [sigma_{k(j)} >= t_j] >= T]. So #SAT(C) = sum_{sigma in G} N(sigma) h(sigma), where N(sigma) = #{x : s(x) = sigma}. DP: A_0 = indicator of the origin on G; A_i(sigma) = A_{i-1}(sigma) + A_{i-1}(sigma - a_i) (entries outside G are dropped). Invariant: A_i(sigma) = #{y in {0,1}^i : sum_{l<=i} y_l a_l = sigma} for sigma in G. Induction step: a vector y in {0,1}^i with partial sum sigma either has y_i=0 (counted by A_{i-1}(sigma)) or y_i=1 (counted by A_{i-1}(sigma - a_i)). No mass is lost by the truncation to G, because every partial sum over l <= i has |coordinate q| <= sum_l |F_{ql}| <= R_q, so each partial sum lies in G. Hence A_n = N on G, and the output sum_{sigma in G} A_n(sigma) h(sigma) equals #SAT(C). Cost: the DP does n steps, each O(|G|) with d-dimensional slicing; evaluating h on a cell costs O(m). All numbers are at most 2^n, so the arithmetic is exact.

COROLLARY (sub-exponential saving). Let B be a constant and d <= n / (4 log2(2Bn+1)). Then |G| <= (2Bn+1)^d <= 2^{n/4}, so #SAT(C) is computed in time poly(n, m) * 2^{n/4} (plus the O(m d n) work to find the distinct rows), against brute force 2^n * poly(n, m). The saving is at least 3n/4 - O(log n) bits, so saving/log n -> infinity: this meets the Lemma 3.8 threshold for this subclass. Outside the subclass (d large) the bound (2Bn+1)^d is not better than 2^n and the lemma gives nothing.

SCOPE / WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this is a proved algorithm for the subclass 'few distinct bottom weight rows, bounded weights, d <= n/(4 log(2Bn+1))'. It does NOT handle random or general THR o THR (d = m there), so it does not repair the general memo-key obstacle. Whether the subclass is a real intermediate step (lane D / lane C, owner's intermediate-goal rule) is for review. It also does not bear on P vs NP without the general lower-bound or CAPP chain.

OPEN after this step: (a) general d with bounded weights, i.e. remove the distinct-rows hypothesis by replacing rows with a low-dimensional approximation (lane D); (b) the same key (sum-vector) for MAJ o MAJ / CAPP (Q-2f96f7e0f1).

structure.lemma: FEW-FORMS LEMMA (repair of G0002: the memo key is replaced, not the variable order). Setting: THR o THR circuit C on n variables with m bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], W_j in Z^n, t_j in Z, and top gate f(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T], v_j in Z, T in Z. Assume the rows W_j take at most d distinct values: W_j = F^{(k(j))} for a matrix F in Z^{d x n} and k: [m] -> [d], and |F_{qi}| <= B. Put R_q = sum_i |F_{qi}| <= B n and grid G = prod_q [-R_q, R_q]. Claim: #SAT(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computed exactly by the DP below in O(n d |G| + m |G|) integer operations, where |G| = prod_q (2R_q+1) <= (2Bn+1)^d.
